rules_evidence.establishes: The game-winner contract settles on which team wins the named game; with no ties in the NBA a win necessarily includes any overtime, and the game is identified by its original schedule date.

rules_evidence.quote: If San Antonio wins by more than 37.5 points in the San Antonio vs Portland Pro Basketball game originally scheduled for Nov 7, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: The spread contract is a one-sided 'wins by more than X.5' threshold on the named team's final margin, with half-point strikes (no push) and rungs far into the tail (37.5).

rules_evidence.quote: If the game is postponed but begins within 48 hours of its originally scheduled start time, the market will remain open and resolve based on the official final result.
rules_evidence.establishes: The spread settles on the official final result; a short postponement keeps the market open and a longer one voids at fair price (same clause as KXNBAGAME).

variants_and_edge_cases: Scope after reconciliation: only the single-game winner (KXNBAGAME) and spread (KXNBASPREAD) series are filed here; series-state, Cup-group, head-to-head and win-margin tickers belong to other archetypes.

Spread strikes are half-points ('wins by more than 37.5'), so no push; each team carries its own one-sided ladder and P(team A wins by > x) for x < 0 is not offered as such, so the two teams' ladders together trace one margin CDF.
Cup (in-season tournament) games and play-in games count as ordinary games for margin, but the Cup final is a separate game for some other props, so the specific game identity matters.

Scope: every input in this record is pregame-knowable. The game markets trade live, but in-play state (score, clock, fouls, lineup on court) is out of scope here and needs its own state-conditioned model.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official final result of the game (the rules' wording); NBA.com game summary / box score as the practical source.

mechanism.summary: A moneyline or spread market is a statement about the distribution of the final margin D = Score_home - Score_away, which is a sum over roughly 200 possessions of efficiency differences plus home court, rest and who is actually on the floor. The mean of D is the difference of two active-roster ratings, so the first-order question is which players play and how many minutes their replacements absorb; the second is how much of each team's rating is luck (three-point shooting, close-game record) rather than ability; the third is matchup and scheme, which moves efficiency at equal ratings; and the fourth is the variance shape, because the margin sd (about 12) depends on pace and totals and the cover probability depends on the sd as much as on the mean. P(win) = P(D>0) including overtime, and the spread ladder is a set of cut points on one density, so rung probabilities must be monotone. Information arrives in discrete bursts (injury report, starters, reporter tweets), and many edges are timing edges around those bursts, not rating edges.

stages.name: Active set and minutes redistribution
stages.description: Margin starts with who plays: each team's active set is a mixture over star in/out scenarios when statuses are questionable, and an absence moves minutes to replacements of a different quality, so the loss is not the star's rating but the gap between star and the marginal replacement times the minutes absorbed. Two absences are not additive because bench depth is exhausted and rotation changes (a thin guard rotation compresses the replacement quality).
stages.distribution: Discrete scenario mixture with 2-4 branches per team; conditional on branch, margin is approximately normal. Absence cost is convex in the number of missing starters.

stages.name: Baseline team strength with luck regression
stages.description: The base rating is an opponent-adjusted offence and defence estimate whose window and shrinkage decide how much recent form is credited. Rating built from games with different rosters is contaminated, so the weight of each past game should reflect how similar its active set was to tonight's. Three-point shooting on both sides and close-game record are only partly skill, so raw ratings must be pulled toward shot-quality-based expectations.
stages.distribution: Rating estimates carry sd of roughly 1.5-2.5 points of margin early in the season, shrinking with games; luck components regress by a large fraction within 20 games.

stages.name: Matchup, scheme and venue
stages.description: At equal ratings, scheme interactions matter: a drop-coverage defence against a pick-and-roll-heavy offence, a team that lives on threes against a switching defence, and rim protection against rim-attack teams change efficiency. Home court adds roughly two points on average, with larger effects at altitude, and with rest and travel adjustments applying to both teams. In the playoffs the star-versus-defender match-ups gain weight because rotations tighten.
stages.distribution: Additive shifts on the margin mean of about 0-3 points; scheme interactions have small sd across opponents and are weakly identified.

stages.name: Motivation and series state
stages.description: Late-season stakes (clinched seed, tanking, seeding races) change who plays and with what effort, while in a playoff series games are not independent: coaching adjustments, injuries accumulating and the pressure of elimination shift the margin from game to game. For a single playoff game priced here, the series state (elimination, a game after a blowout loss, home/away swing) conditions that game's margin mean.
stages.distribution: Regime change in availability late in the season; series-level correlation between games of a few points of margin.

stages.name: Margin distribution and settlement transform
stages.description: The final margin is approximately normal with sd 11-13 but with lump near zero from overtime (tied regulation adds 5 minutes) and fat tails from garbage-time collapse; sd scales with pace and total, so a high-total game has a wider margin distribution at the same mean. P(win) and spread cover are the same density evaluated at different cut points, and win-margin bands are differences between them, so a single density must be consistent across all these markets.
stages.distribution: Mixture of a normal body, an OT-induced local mass near zero and heavier tails when a team is a heavy favourite; heteroscedastic in pace/total.

availability_news.note: Vintage and calibrated resolution of questionable players.

game_context_script.note: OT mass, pace-dependent variance and series state.

pace_volume.note: Possession count scales the margin variance; pace has no direct effect on the mean.

efficiency_conversion.note: Luck regression on shooting and close games.

officiating_rules.note: Referee crew effects on home bias and foul rates are not attached to this archetype even though nba.referee_crew exists; evidence for a crew effect on margin (as opposed to totals) is weak and unresolved.

settlement_contract.note: Both series have rules text: winner of the named game (no ties, OT implicit) and 'wins by more than X.5' spread; 48-hour postponement rule, fair-price void otherwise. Spread OT inclusion is implied by 'official final result' but not explicit (u1).

nba.nonadditive_absence_curve.label: Non-additive multi-absence cost curve
nba.nonadditive_absence_curve.mechanism: The margin cost of losing several rotation players is not the sum of individual costs because the replacement pool deteriorates and rotations compress.
nba.nonadditive_absence_curve.rationale: The existing catalog sums per-player impact (player_impact, lineup_adj_rating) but missing two starters on a team with a deep bench costs less than two times one, whereas on a thin team it costs more; the curve must be estimated by roster depth.
nba.nonadditive_absence_curve.measurement: Fit on 5 seasons of team-games: margin residual vs number of missing rotation players (top-8 by minutes) and the sum of their impact values, with spline in missing impact and interaction with depth index (average impact of players 9-12); predictions per scenario branch; shrink spline with ridge; as-of nightly after injury report.
nba.nonadditive_absence_curve.why: Questionable-star mixtures and multi-injury nights are exactly where linear impact sums misprice.

nba.replacement_level_minutes_absorption.label: Replacement-level minutes absorption
nba.replacement_level_minutes_absorption.mechanism: When a rotation player is out, minutes flow to specific teammates at specific quality; who absorbs them (a starter playing more versus a bench player starting) determines the actual rating loss.
nba.replacement_level_minutes_absorption.rationale: Impact-based absence valuations assume replacement at team-average bench quality; a team whose next man up is a two-way player or an out-of-position player loses much more.
nba.replacement_level_minutes_absorption.measurement: From 3 seasons of game-level minutes: for each team and absent role (primary ball handler, wing, rim protector), estimate the share of vacated minutes absorbed by each teammate with ridge regression, then compute expected replaced rating = Σ share_j × impact_j(minutes-adjusted); use 20-game half-life; compare to team default; fallback to position-group priors for new combinations.
nba.replacement_level_minutes_absorption.why: Gives the second half of the absence cost; the player_impact input only covers the missing player's rating.

nba.roster_overlap_weighted_rating.label: Roster-overlap weighted team rating
nba.roster_overlap_weighted_rating.mechanism: Past game results are weighted by how similar the active set of that game was to tonight's, so results from games with different rosters count less.
nba.roster_overlap_weighted_rating.rationale: Season ratings blend games played with and without stars, and a rating from a healthy-roster sample misleads for a depleted lineup; the overlap weighting makes the baseline condition on the rotation.
nba.roster_overlap_weighted_rating.measurement: Weight w_g = exp(-lambda × (1 - overlap_g)) × recency half-life 40 games, overlap_g = Σ over tonight's top-10 players of min_share_tonight × I(played in game g), lambda fit by out-of-sample game-margin error on 3 seasons; rating = weighted opponent-adjusted net rating shrunk to the preseason prior with k=15 effective games.
nba.roster_overlap_weighted_rating.why: Without it, lineup_adj_rating and off/def ratings mix incompatible samples and over-credit healthy-roster results.

nba.margin_heteroscedasticity.label: Pace- and total-dependent margin standard deviation (own-model, not line-based)
nba.margin_heteroscedasticity.mechanism: Margin variance scales with possession count and total scoring, and with spread through garbage time.
nba.margin_heteroscedasticity.rationale: The existing score_resid is defined around lines, which is market-derived; the variance should come from the game's own pace/total estimates so that cover probabilities at wide spreads are correct.
nba.margin_heteroscedasticity.measurement: Fit sd_margin = a + b × sqrt(own-model possessions) + c × |own-model mean margin| on 5 seasons of team-games (own predictions, not closing lines); report quantile curves (10/25/50/75/90) with a skew parameter for heavy favourites; validate by the probability integral transform per bucket.
raw_data: Walk-forward own-model mean margin and possessions
nba.margin_heteroscedasticity.why: A margin sd off by one point moves a 6-10 point band by about 1.2 percentage points and P(win) by about 1.4 points at a 6-point mean margin (sd 12 versus 13), so sd matters but far less than a 3-4 point rung error.

nba.series_game_conditional_state.label: Playoff-series game-conditional state
nba.series_game_conditional_state.mechanism: In a series, a game's mean margin depends on series score, rest days between games, accumulated injuries and coaching adjustments.
nba.series_game_conditional_state.rationale: Single-game ratings treat games as independent; series markets (home clinch, game 7, comeback) depend on the dependency between games and on elimination-state minutes tightening.
nba.series_game_conditional_state.measurement: Model for game g of a series: margin_residual = actual margin - own-model pre-game expected margin (ratings plus home advantage, as of tipoff, from nba.ratings) regressed on rest days since the last game, elimination-game indicator for the trailing team, injury-status change since game 1 (minutes-weighted impact of newly absent players), previous game's margin (shrunk) and games played, on playoff series 2000-2025 with a series random intercept; estimate the sd of the random intercept by REML (do not assume 2 points) and report its posterior. Update the series effect after each completed game by a normal-normal step. Output a mean shift and sd for the next game. As-of: last completed game and the injury report vintage.
raw_data: series game logs with margin, minutes, rest days
nba.series_game_conditional_state.why: Series-level markets in this archetype have no mechanism in the draft; the random effect sets the correlation of outcomes between games.

nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.label: Own-model regulation tie probability P(OT)
nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.mechanism: P(OT) = mass of regulation margin at zero from a heteroscedastic margin density with a late-game excess-mass correction.
nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.rationale: The draft claims P(OT) is roughly flat across spreads, but a Gaussian with sd 12 gives 3.3% at pick-em and 2.3% at 10 points, so the dependence on spread is large; the right model is a decreasing function with an empirical excess factor.
nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.measurement: P_gauss(0) = phi(mu/sigma)/sigma with mu own-model margin and sigma from own ratings and pace (nba.lineup_adj_rating and nba.pace; about 12, scaling with sqrt(possessions)); multiply by excess factor kappa(|mu|) estimated by isotonic regression on 10 seasons of games as observed OT rate divided by P_gauss(0) in |mu| buckets of 2 points; kappa about 1.7-1.9 overall; output with beta interval; use own-model mu, not closing lines. Margin is integer-valued with parity tied to the total, and free-throw, three-point and intentional-foul structure moves mass onto and off zero, so estimate the observed integer pmf at 0 (and smoothed mass at +/-1 to +/-4) over 15 seasons and let kappa(|mu|) absorb the discreteness rather than reading the continuous density at zero.
nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.why: Market-free probability that regulation ends tied, from the own-model margin mean and sd with an integer-pmf excess at zero; needed because overtime changes the settled quantity.
raw_data: team-game regulation and final scores with period counts (15 seasons)
own-model expected margin and sd per game

nba.lineup_adj_rating.reason: Closest to the right target (active-set rating), but built from season ratings without roster-overlap weighting or replacement-quality modelling.

nba.off_rtg.reason: Opponent-adjusted offence is a component of lineup_adj_rating, so it is partly redundant; keep because offence and defence behave differently for pace and variance.

nba.def_rtg.reason: Defence is noisier than offence and more luck-affected (opponent 3P%), so shrink harder; overlaps with lineup_adj_rating.

nba.player_impact.reason: Needed to translate an absence into points, but valid only combined with the replacement and non-additivity terms; impact estimates have large sd for low-minute players.

nba.injuries_pit.reason: The single most time-sensitive input; the vintage relative to the market quote determines whether the price is stale.

nba.status_resolution_prob.reason: Calibrated P(plays | questionable) supplies scenario weights; the calibration by status, age and rest is the value, not the label.

nba.starters_pit.reason: Confirmed lineup arrives about 30 minutes pre-tip, after most liquidity; useful for late trading and as a label for status resolution.

nba.load_mgmt.reason: Rest probability for stars on back-to-backs; overlaps with status_resolution_prob where a rest status is posted, but explains resting before it is listed.

nba.rest_travel.reason: Rest differential and back-to-back are the cleanest schedule effects; the draft combines altitude here as well.

nba.travel_altitude.reason: The rest_travel input already lists altitude and travel in its definition; the separate entry measures the same schedule-environment effect.

nba.venue.reason: Home court is worth roughly two points on average but varies by team and has fallen over time; a constant misses team-specific effects.

nba.standings_motivation.reason: Matters mostly in the last 15 games and mainly through who plays, which the availability inputs already capture.

nba.three_pt_luck.reason: Regressing hot or cold three-point shooting is the standard rating correction; effect is bounded by the share of threes in the team's shot diet.

nba.pythag_residual.reason: Records luck in close games; only relevant if the model uses records, not margin-based ratings, so low incremental value.

nba.score_resid.reason: Defined around lines (a market quantity); the residual distribution should be built from own-model predictions to avoid circularity, replaced by margin_heteroscedasticity.

nba.ot_model.reason: Catalog measurement is an empirical P(OT) by |spread| bucket and total bucket, keyed on market lines, so it is a benchmark; the own-model nba.reg_tie_pmf_model supplies P(OT).

nba.onoff.reason: On/off data are noisy and confounded by teammates; as a validator of lineup rating it is useful, but not an input to the mean.

nba.def_scheme.reason: Scheme interaction exists but is weakly identified in the regular season; useful mainly in series.

nba.matchup_def.reason: Individual defender assignments are partly unknowable pregame and the same information is in scheme; small incremental value outside the playoffs.

m.quote_history.reason: Kalshi price path for the game winner and spread ladder; useful to see when information was absorbed and for calibration labels, but it is an observation of the market, never an explanatory driver of the outcome.

m.rules_text.reason: Versioned rules text defines the settled quantity for the game winner and spread ladder; wording changes between series are the only way to know the target variable, so it is a required contract input, not a feature.

m.external_lines.reason: Sharp closing spread and moneyline are the efficient benchmark; a model that takes them as input cannot show an edge, so use for comparison only.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Cross-rung monotonicity of the game winner and spread ladder is derived from Kalshi prices, so it flags stale quotes (an execution diagnostic) and carries no information about the underlying result.

m.orderbook_depth.reason: Depth and spread on the game winner and spread ladder set tradable size and minimum edge; they come from the market itself and say nothing about the event mechanism.

m.fees.reason: Fee schedule converts a probability gap into net edge for the game winner and spread ladder; needed for decision thresholds only, constant with respect to the outcome.

nba.market_calibration_bias.reason: Price-bucket miscalibration for the game winner and spread ladder is measured on Kalshi prices, so it is a market-derived correction layer applied after a probability exists, not an input.

m.volume_oi.reason: Volume/open interest for the game winner and spread ladder measures liquidity and attention; market-derived and not a driver of the outcome, usable only to discount thin quotes.

m.trade_tape.reason: Trade prints for the game winner and spread ladder are market microstructure; informed-flow inference from them is speculative and cannot be a causal input.

m.settlement_truth.reason: Settled value and timestamp for the game winner and spread ladder are labels for calibration and need reconciling against the named source; not a pregame input.

nba.garbage.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (interaction on nba.score_resid x nba.garbage: Large spreads change margin variance; at -12 and beyond cover probability depends on late bench minutes.) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

interactions.mechanism: A questionable star creates a two-point mixture whose mean differs by several points, so the market price may match only one branch; with two questionable players the branches multiply and the cost is non-additive, so the mixture cannot be reduced to an expected rating.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute the model probability as a mixture and compare to using the expected rating; test on nights with two or more questionable starters.

interactions.mechanism: The back-to-back effect is mostly a star-rest effect; conditional on all stars playing, the direct fatigue effect on margin is small (around a point) and larger for older rosters.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress margin residual on back-to-back with and without controlling for the active-set rating; test an age-by-b2b term.

interactions.mechanism: Cover probability at a given spread depends on mean/sd, and sd rises with pace and total while the mean is set by ratings, so a fast game with a large favourite covers a wide spread less often than a slow game with the same mean.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate cover probabilities in a grid of (mean margin, sd) and compare to a constant-sd normal in out-of-sample games.

interactions.mechanism: Rating correction for hot three-point shooting is proportional to the team's three-point attempt rate: a team with 45% of shots from three has more luck variance to remove than one with 30%.
interactions.how_to_test: Test whether the regression coefficient of future margin on past 3P% residual scales with 3PA rate.

interactions.mechanism: In a series, defensive scheme adjustments after game 2-3 reduce the offence's advantage, so a regular-season matchup edge decays across games; the effect is regime-dependent on whether the coach changes the coverage.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the matchup-edge coefficient by game number within series.

nonlinearities.shape: Probit link from expected margin to win probability
nonlinearities.why: P(win) = Φ(mean/sd) is concave in the favourite's mean margin above about 8 points, so a one-point rating error matters more for near-even games than for heavy favourites.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex in number of missing rotation players
nonlinearities.why: The cost of each additional absence grows as depth runs out, so a linear sum of impacts understates multi-injury nights.

nonlinearities.shape: Concave in rest days: large first back-to-back penalty, flat beyond 2 days
nonlinearities.why: A game on zero days' rest costs about a point, one day of rest nearly erases it, and extra days add little.

nonlinearities.shape: Local point mass at zero margin
nonlinearities.why: Regulation ties convert into overtime and a margin of a few points, producing a spike in the density just around zero that a continuous normal misses.

contract.settlement_definition: Six live series: five with recovered rules text and one (KXNBABENCHPTS, re-filed here on 2026-11-09 from player_points) with none. KXNBAOT: Yes if at least 1 overtime period is played in the named game (48-hour postponement rule, fair price if cancelled or not started within 48 hours). KXNBAOVERTIME: Yes if the two teams 'go to overtime' in the named game (same event; no postponement clause in its text). KXNBASERIESOT: Yes if at least N games (sampled: 3+) go to overtime in a named playoff series (sampled: the Finals), i.e. a count threshold over a random-length series, not a single indicator. KXNBAH2HBENCHPTS and KXNBAH2HTEAM3PT: Yes if team A records more total bench points / more made three-pointers than team B 'in the full game'; an exact tie resolves 50/50; a game cancelled or postponed more than two weeks resolves to a fair market price. KXNBABENCHPTS (title 'NBA Bench Points', series scope 'Bench Points', basis NO_LISTING: no market ever listed; evidence is the title and scope string only) is TITLE_ONLY and its entity is UNRESOLVED: BASKETBALLENTITYSTAT.pdf is also the terms file of player-prop series (KXNBAPTS, KXNBAREB), so it does not show a team total; it is modelled here as a team's non-starter points (the quantity the sibling head-to-head KXNBAH2HBENCHPTS compares by its sampled rules, which are context, not KXNBABENCHPTS rules), while its strike construction, bench definition, overtime treatment and tie rule are unseen. Not stated: whether 'full game' includes overtime (likely, not explicit), the definition of 'bench' (official non-starters), and stat-correction handling (u1, u4).

rules_evidence.quote: If at least 1 overtime period is played in the Miami vs Sacramento Pro Basketball game originally scheduled for Nov 8, 2026
rules_evidence.establishes: The single-game overtime contract is an indicator that regulation ended tied: one overtime is enough, extra periods do not change the result, and the game is identified by its original schedule date.

rules_evidence.quote: If at least 3 games go to overtime in the New York vs San Antonio Pro Basketball Finals series in the 2026 Pro Basketball Playoffs, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: The series overtime contract is a count threshold (3+ overtime games) over all games of one named series, so series length and within-series dependence of close games drive it.

rules_evidence.quote: If both teams record an equal number of total bench points, then all markets resolve to 50/50.
rules_evidence.establishes: An exact bench-points tie pays 50/50, so P(Yes-equivalent) = P(A>B) + 0.5 P(A=B) and the tie mass enters linearly.

rules_evidence.quote: If San Antonio records more made three pointers than New York in the full game of the New York vs San Antonio professional basketball game
rules_evidence.establishes: The team three-pointer head-to-head compares made threes over the 'full game' (overtime inclusion implied, not explicit); ties resolve 50/50 by the same secondary clause.

rules_evidence.quote: If the game is cancelled or postponed more than two weeks, then all markets resolve to a fair market price.
rules_evidence.establishes: Head-to-head team-stat markets use a two-week postponement window, unlike the 48-hour window of KXNBAOT.

rules_evidence.quote: If New York and San Antonio go to overtime in the New York vs San Antonio professional basketball game originally scheduled for Jun 13, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: KXNBAOVERTIME is the same single-game overtime indicator as KXNBAOT under a second ticker family.

variants_and_edge_cases: Single-game overtime (KXNBAOT, KXNBAOVERTIME) is an indicator of regulation ending tied; multiple overtimes do not change the result.

Series overtime (KXNBASERIESOT) is a count threshold ('at least 3 games' in the sampled Finals market): with per-game P(OT) near 6%, P(>=3 of 4-7 games) is a rare tail event (order 1%) dominated by series length and within-series closeness correlation; other thresholds (1+, 2+) may be listed.

Head-to-head ties resolve 50/50 (both bench points and team threes); for team threes (means about 12-15 per team) the exact-tie mass is about 7-9%, for bench points (sd of the difference near 11) about 3-4%.
'Full game' is not defined: overtime most likely counts, adding roughly 5 minutes of starter-heavy play (bench share low), which matters for bench points more than for threes (u1).
Bench definition: bench points are points by players who did not start; a late starter change promotes a reserve out of the bench count. The rules do not name the source for starter designation (u4).
Postponement windows differ inside the archetype: 48 hours for KXNBAOT, two weeks for the head-to-heads, unstated for KXNBAOVERTIME and KXNBASERIESOT.

KXNBABENCHPTS (no listed market; title and scope string only): the entity is unresolved, either a team's non-starter points (modelled here, probably an over/under or ladder on one team's total) or a named player's points as a bench player; its terms file BASKETBALLENTITYSTAT.pdf is the same one used by player-prop series and differs from the head-to-head file BASKETBALLH2H.pdf, so tie, overtime and postponement handling cannot be copied from KXNBAH2HBENCHPTS.

The Kalshi series metadata for KXNBABENCHPTS (retrieved 2026-11-09) lists ESPN and the Governing League (nba.com) as settlement sources.

mechanism.summary: Overtime is the event that regulation margin equals zero, so its probability is the probability mass of the end-of-regulation margin distribution at a single integer. With margin approximately normal with mean mu (the own-model expected margin, not the closing spread) and sd sigma near 12, that mass is phi(mu/sigma)/sigma, about 3.3% at a pick-em, falling to about 2.3% at a 10-point expected margin and about 1.7% at 14; the observed overall rate is higher, near 6%, because end-of-game strategy (tie-seeking threes, intentional fouling and clock management) piles extra probability at zero and small margins. So P(OT) is strongly decreasing in |spread|, not flat, and is higher for slow, low-variance games. Bench-points markets (the head-to-head KXNBAH2HBENCHPTS, whose rules are sampled, and KXNBABENCHPTS, whose entity is unresolved and is read here as a team's total only as a working assumption) are different: the outcome is the sum of points from non-starters, a function of how many minutes the bench plays (240 minus starter minutes, plus 25 in OT), the bench's points per minute, and the official starter list that defines who counts. Team-stat head-to-heads compare two correlated counts (the pace shared by both teams creates positive correlation), so the sign and size of the difference depend on volumes and rates, not on a margin tie mass.

stages.name: Regulation margin density at zero
stages.description: P(OT) equals the probability that the regulation margin lands on 0. With the mean set by availability-adjusted ratings and the sd set by pace and the favourite's size, the Gaussian body gives the baseline mass at zero, and that mass shrinks roughly like exp(-mu^2 / (2 sigma^2)); a 12-point favourite is about 40% less likely to need overtime than a pick-em. Slow, low-total games have smaller sigma and so slightly more mass at zero.
stages.distribution: Single-integer mass of a near-normal density, about 3.3% at a pick-em from the Gaussian alone; heteroscedastic in pace; empirical excess to about 6% overall from late-game structure.

stages.name: Late-game tie-forcing strategy
stages.description: In the last minute, the trailing team down by three can attempt a tying three, the leading team can foul to prevent it or defend the three, and clock management determines possessions left. Intentional fouling turns near-ties into free-throw sequences whose outcomes concentrate at margins of 1-4 points. This end-of-game structure puts probability exactly on zero that a smooth margin model misses, and the amount depends on coach policy, free-throw shooting of the ball handlers and whether the team leads by 3.
stages.distribution: Excess point mass at 0 and at +/-1 to 3 compared to a Gaussian; amount is policy-dependent and not captured by ratings.

stages.name: Overtime length and what it adds
stages.description: Given overtime, the game adds one five-minute period (about 22-26 total points) with a second OT in a minority of overtime games, adding starter-heavy minutes to both teams, which changes the starter/bench split and the team stat counts for the head-to-heads if 'full game' includes OT. KXNBASERIESOT asks for at least N overtime games (3+ in the Finals sample) across a best-of-seven: the count is a Poisson-binomial over a random number of games (4 to 7) with per-game tie probabilities from each game's own-model margin, inflated by positive within-series correlation of closeness; at p near 6% the 3+ event sits deep in the tail, so the dispersion parameter and the series-length distribution matter more than the mean OT rate.
stages.distribution: OT periods: geometric-like with P(second OT | first OT) about 0.07-0.10; series OT-game count: overdispersed Poisson-binomial mixture over series length, P(>=3) of order 1%.

stages.name: Bench minutes and bench scoring rate (head-to-head, and a team total if that is the entity)
stages.description: Bench points = bench minutes times bench points per minute. Bench minutes are what is left after the starters' minutes, which fall in blowouts and when foul trouble hits, and rise when a starter is out and the bench is deep. The points per minute reflect bench scorers' usage, which depends on whether a sixth man is a primary scorer and on the second unit's lineup. The definition of bench via the starter list moves the target when a starter is rested. If KXNBABENCHPTS is a team total (unresolved; a player-level reading is not excluded) the target is one team's own total rather than a difference, so the full distribution of that total (mean 30-40 in the usual state, a right tail in blowouts, a mixture over which five start) is needed, and nba.team_bench_points_model assembles it from projected starter minutes, reserve scoring rates and the margin path; the head-to-head series use the difference of two such totals.
stages.distribution: Bench points have sd about 8 around means of about 35 points; strongly state-dependent (blowout state shifts bench minutes by 20+). Non-negative, right-skewed.

stages.name: Team-stat pair distribution
stages.description: KXNBAH2HTEAM3PT compares team A and team B made threes; each count is team three-point attempts (team 3PA rate per possession against the opponent's 3PA allowed, times shared possessions) times a make rate regressed toward shot quality. The counts are positively correlated through shared pace and negatively through score state (the trailing team takes more threes late), so the difference is narrower than independent counts. The 50/50 tie rule means the 7-9% exact-tie mass is split, and overtime adds attempts to both sides.
stages.distribution: Difference of two overdispersed counts with correlation about +0.2 to 0.3 from shared pace; discrete with a mass at zero.

talent_strength.note: Team ratings fix the mean margin (for tie mass) and scoring volumes (for stat pairs).

opponent_matchup.note: Opponent-allowed rates for the head-to-head team stat.

role_personnel.note: Who starts defines who is bench; the team bench-points model converts the starting five and reserve rates into a team total for KXNBAH2HBENCHPTS and, under the unresolved team-total reading, KXNBABENCHPTS.

availability_news.note: Starter absences promote bench players and change the definition.

environment.note: Venue and altitude have a tiny effect on the tie mass at zero or on bench share, whose determinants are margin spread and substitution patterns; no environmental input is warranted.

pace_volume.note: Pace scales sd of margin and counts; bench minutes are the volume for bench points.

efficiency_conversion.note: Shooting variance matters for team-stat pairs but does not forecast OT.

distribution_variance.note: Point mass at zero margin and the count-difference distribution.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest, rotation tightening in the playoffs and rested starters change bench minutes and OT structure, but no input in the archetype links schedule situation to bench share or to tie-forcing strategy.

officiating_rules.note: Referee calls shape foul rates and thus late-game free throws, but the dependence of overtime on officiating is second-order relative to margin density; the only rule item is the overtime format (five minutes), which is constant.

settlement_contract.note: Five of the six series have rules text (KXNBABENCHPTS has none): game OT indicator (two tickers), series OT count threshold (3+ in the Finals sample), head-to-head bench points and team threes with 50/50 ties and a two-week postponement window. 'Full game' OT inclusion and bench source are not stated (u1, u4).

nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.label: Own-model regulation tie probability P(OT)
nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.mechanism: P(OT) = mass of regulation margin at zero from a heteroscedastic margin density with a late-game excess-mass correction.
nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.rationale: The draft claims P(OT) is roughly flat across spreads, but a Gaussian with sd 12 gives 3.3% at pick-em and 2.3% at 10 points, so the dependence on spread is large; the right model is a decreasing function with an empirical excess factor.
nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.measurement: P_gauss(0) = phi(mu/sigma)/sigma with mu own-model margin and sigma from own ratings and pace (nba.lineup_adj_rating and nba.pace; about 12, scaling with sqrt(possessions)); multiply by excess factor kappa(|mu|) estimated by isotonic regression on 10 seasons of games as observed OT rate divided by P_gauss(0) in |mu| buckets of 2 points; kappa about 1.7-1.9 overall; output with beta interval; use own-model mu, not closing lines. Margin is integer-valued with parity tied to the total, and free-throw, three-point and intentional-foul structure moves mass onto and off zero, so estimate the observed integer pmf at 0 (and smoothed mass at +/-1 to +/-4) over 15 seasons and let kappa(|mu|) absorb the discreteness rather than reading the continuous density at zero.
raw_data: team-game regulation and final scores with period counts (15 seasons)
own-model expected margin and sd per game
nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.why: Overtime is the whole contract in KXNBAOT and the density-at-zero formulation gives the correct dependence on spread and pace.

nba.last_possession_tie_attempt_rate.label: Coach-level tie-forcing and intentional-foul policy
nba.last_possession_tie_attempt_rate.mechanism: How often a team trailing by 2-3 in the last 30 seconds attempts a tying three or a fast two, and how often the leading team fouls up three.
nba.last_possession_tie_attempt_rate.rationale: Excess tie mass comes from end-of-game choices; teams differ, and the same game state yields a tie more often when the trailing coach shoots for the tie than when he fouls and hopes.
nba.last_possession_tie_attempt_rate.measurement: From play-by-play: in games within 3 points with <30 seconds left, share of trailing-team possessions ending in a 3PA, a 2PA or a foul-drawn FT; leading-team foul-up-3 rate; compute per coach over 3 seasons (min 15 events) with shrinkage k=10 events to league mean; produce per-matchup tie-conditional probability = P(close at 30s) × P(tie | close, policies).
nba.last_possession_tie_attempt_rate.why: Gives the excess zero mass a coach-level driver.

nba.ot_period_distribution.label: Distribution of number of overtime periods and OT scoring
nba.ot_period_distribution.mechanism: If overtime occurs, additional periods occur with a small probability and each period adds a fixed block of minutes and points.
nba.ot_period_distribution.rationale: The count of OT periods matters for series OT markets and for strike markets on total, bench or team stats within the family; the draft treats OT as one event.
nba.ot_period_distribution.measurement: Empirical P(k OT periods) from 15 seasons: P(1), P(2), P(3+) conditional on OT; per-period points per team sampled from the league distribution adjusted for pace (mean about 11-12 per team per 5 minutes, sd 5); update yearly; for series OT: P(at least one OT game) = sum over series length L of P(L) * (1 - prod over games g of (1 - p_g)), with P(L) from nba.series_model (4-7 games, shorter for mismatched teams) and p_g from nba.reg_tie_pmf_model using each game's own-model margin; inflate the variance across games because closeness is positively correlated within a series (estimate by the observed share of series with >=1 OT game versus the independent prediction on 15 seasons of playoff series). The settled quantity (at least one OT game, or a count) is unsampled, see u6.
raw_data: Game period counts and OT scores
nba.ot_period_distribution.why: Distinguishes first from second OT for team-stat targets and gives the per-period OT block; the series count tail is carried by nba.series_ot_count_model.

nba.bench_minutes_distribution.label: Bench minutes distribution (240 + 25k minus starter minutes)
nba.bench_minutes_distribution.mechanism: Bench points depend on bench minutes first; they equal total team minutes minus starter minutes and shrink when starters play heavy minutes in close games or OT.
nba.bench_minutes_distribution.rationale: The draft's bench input is points share, while the better predictor is minutes times points per minute with a state-dependent minutes distribution.
nba.bench_minutes_distribution.measurement: Per team: bench minutes = 240 + 25*OT - Σ starter minutes; model starter minutes as scenario mixture (blowout/close/OT/foul trouble) with weights from own-model margin; bench points = bench minutes × bench points-per-minute with 30-game half-life and shrinkage k=300 minutes; as-of lineups; output mean/sd by scenario.
free_sources: nba_api box score minutes and starters
nba.bench_minutes_distribution.why: A bench-points strike is a minutes question first; blowout and OT regimes shift it by 15-25 minutes.

nba.starter_bench_definition_ledger.label: Starter/bench designation ledger and rest-driven reclassification
nba.starter_bench_definition_ledger.mechanism: The bench is the set of players not in the official starting five, so a starter absence promotes the next man into the starter group and shifts scoring from bench to starter.
nba.starter_bench_definition_ledger.rationale: The draft interaction says a rested starter becomes a bench player, but a rested starter does not play; the real effects are (a) a promoted bench player moves out of the bench count and (b) a returning star on a restriction coming off the bench moves in.
nba.starter_bench_definition_ledger.measurement: Record for each team-game: official starters list, status of expected starters, bench designation of the primary scorers; compute counterfactual bench points under tonight's starter list using player points-per-minute and projected minutes: bench_pts = Σ_{non-starters} proj_min × ppm; adjust for returning player minute limits; as-of lineup confirmation.
nba.starter_bench_definition_ledger.why: The market's definition of bench changes with the starter list so the estimate must be conditional on the list.

nba.team_stat_pair_difference_model.label: Team-stat pair difference model (shared-pace correlation)
nba.team_stat_pair_difference_model.mechanism: The head-to-head team stat is the difference of two counts with positive correlation through game pace and negative through script effects.
nba.team_stat_pair_difference_model.rationale: Treating the two teams' counts as independent overstates the sd of the difference and misprices the zero-tie mass.
nba.team_stat_pair_difference_model.measurement: For a team stat X (e.g. 3PM): mean_X = attempts_X x rate_X using opponent-adjusted attempts and rates (20-game half-life, rate shrunk with k=150 attempts); each team's count ~ negative binomial with dispersion estimated from 3 seasons of team-games. Correlation rho between the two teams' counts = empirical correlation of residual counts across the same game over 3 seasons, modelled as a linear function of the game's total possessions (pace) and pooled by stat; use a Gaussian copula with this rho to couple the two NB marginals. Compute P(A>B) and P(tie) by summing the joint pmf; apply the blowout correction by increasing the trailing team's 3PA rate by the coefficient estimated from the margin-conditional attempt rate (nba.three_att_script_elasticity). As-of: games before tip.
raw_data: team-game shot counts (3PA, 3PM, FTA, etc.) and possessions
nba.team_stat_pair_difference_model.why: Team-stat markets inside this family use a different distribution from the tie-mass logic of OT.

nba.series_model.label: Best-of-seven series model (home-court, game-to-game correlation, adjustments)
nba.series_model.mechanism: Series win and game-count probabilities derive from per-game win probabilities with home pattern; correlated injuries and adjustments change the distribution.
nba.series_model.rationale: A simple independent binomial overstates sweeps vs actual; playoff rotations shorten, pace slows, and stars play more minutes, shifting the effective team rating. Series props (sweep, exact games, player series totals) need game-level scoring simulations. Subtle: in-series injuries and coaching adjustments create positive correlation between games.
nba.series_model.measurement: Per-game win p from playoff-adjusted ratings with home advantage; sample game-to-game correlation parameter; adapt rating after injuries; compute pmf of series length and winner.
nba.series_model.why: Best-of-seven length distribution and game-to-game dependence that turn a per-game tie probability into the probability of at least one overtime game in KXNBASERIESOT.

nba.lineup_adj_rating.label: Availability-adjusted team rating for tonight's active set
nba.lineup_adj_rating.mechanism: Team strength given who is actually active, computed by summing player impact over expected minutes, moves spreads, totals and every player prop in the game.
nba.lineup_adj_rating.rationale: A star absence changes team net rating by an amount far larger than most other features; the market reprices within minutes of the report. The model needs an independent player-impact valuation to avoid just reading the market. Subtle: impact of replacing a player is not the star's full value (usage redistributes), and replacement is nonlinear when multiple players are out.
nba.lineup_adj_rating.measurement: For team t and game g: adj_t = sum_i m_i * (I_i - Ibar) where I_i is player i's multi-season ridge RAPM (offence + defence, points per 100 possessions, prior weight 1,500 possessions, as of the day before) for the expected-active players, m_i = projected minutes share (nba.minutes, sums to 1 over the active set) and Ibar the minutes-weighted impact of the team's healthy baseline rotation over the last 30 games. Output in points per 100 possessions, multiply by expected possessions/100 to get points of margin. Validate with with/without team splits when n >= 10 games each. As-of: latest injury-report vintage before tip.
free_sources: PBPStats.com (free tier: on/off, lineup, possession-level splits)
DARKO (darko.app, free web view; no official API)
Dunks & Threes EPM (free partial; no official API)
raw_data: Player impact estimates as of date
nba.lineup_adj_rating.why: Availability-adjusted team rating for the active set; sets the own-model margin mean mu fed to the tie-mass model (replaces the WEAK off_rtg/def_rtg for talent coverage).

nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.label: Ratings-based blowout probability and starter-minutes-vs-margin curve (market-free)
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.mechanism: Rebuilds the blowout risk from team strength and rotation history instead of the closing spread: a ratings-implied expected margin and margin spread give P(large lead), and a coach/player minutes-versus-margin curve converts each margin path into expected minutes lost by starters and gained by bench players.
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.rationale: The catalog input nba.garbage is defined from the closing spread, which is a market price and so a benchmark, not an input. The causal quantity is the chance that the margin passes the coach's pull threshold early enough to matter, and how much playing time each player then loses. Subtle: the loss depends on when the lead arrives (a 20-point lead entering Q4 removes far more starter minutes than one reached with 3 minutes left), on the coach, and on whether the trailing team also pulls starters, so the curve must be conditional on the margin path and not only on the final margin.
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.measurement: Step 1, expected margin: mu = (NetRtg_home_adj - NetRtg_away_adj) * expected_possessions/100 + home_adv, where NetRtg_adj is the as-of-tipoff opponent-adjusted net rating from nba.off_rtg and nba.def_rtg (ridge regression on game point differential, half-life about 25 games, shrunk to the preseason prior with n_prior about 20 games as a placeholder to be fitted), adjusted for the confirmed unavailable players via nba.lineup_adj_rating, home_adv fitted on the last 5 seasons (about 2 points). Step 2, margin spread: sd_margin fitted on 5 seasons of residuals of final margin versus mu (league-wide roughly 12-13 points, to be estimated, with a heavier empirical tail than normal). Step 3: P(final |margin| >= 15/20/25) and P(|lead| >= 15/20 entering Q4) from the empirical residual distribution around mu. Step 4, minutes curve: from play-by-play stints, per team-season, expected minutes of each rotation player conditional on margin entering Q4 in bins (0-9, 10-14, 15-19, 20+), shrunk toward the league curve with k about 30 blowout games. Output per player: expected minutes lost and the probability of falling below a stated minutes level. No closing line or other price is used; the spread is retained only to benchmark calibration of step 3.
free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com leaguegamelog (team game logs, free, undocumented, rate-limited)
cdn.nba.com liveData playbyplay JSON (substitutions with score, free, unofficial)
Basketball-Reference game logs and play-by-play (free, polite scraping)
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.why: Replaces the spread-based nba.garbage in game_overtime_and_team_events: blowout truncation of the relevant players' minutes from own ratings and the coach's pull curve, with no closing line used.
raw_data: team-game final margins and opponent-adjusted ratings as of tipoff (5 seasons)
play-by-play substitution stints with margin entering Q4

nba.team_three_attempt_matchup.label: Team three-point attempt rate versus opponent 3PA allowed
nba.team_three_attempt_matchup.mechanism: Team made threes = possessions x team 3PA per possession x make rate; the 3PA share is a stable team-scheme trait modulated by how many threes the opponent's defence concedes.
nba.team_three_attempt_matchup.rationale: KXNBAH2HTEAM3PT is settled on made threes, and attempt volume (25-45 3PA per team-game across the league) separates teams far more than 3P%; a high-volume team facing a defence that runs opponents off the line loses much of its edge, which ratings and pace inputs do not capture.
nba.team_three_attempt_matchup.measurement: Team 3PA per 100 possessions (EWMA, 15-game half-life, shrunk to team prior season with weight 20 games) multiplied by opponent 3PA-allowed index (opponent 3PA allowed per 100 / league mean, 20-game half-life, shrunk with weight 25 games); expected 3PA = index-adjusted rate x projected game possessions / 100, adjusted for missing high-volume shooters via player 3PA shares; make rate from nba.three_pt_luck expectation; as-of: games completed before the market's snapshot.
free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com team and opponent shooting dashboards
nba.team_three_attempt_matchup.why: Gives each side's expected made-three volume for the team-threes head-to-head, which the generic pair model needs as its means.

nba.series_ot_count_model.label: Series overtime-game count model (threshold tail over random series length)
nba.series_ot_count_model.mechanism: The number of overtime games in a playoff series is a sum of per-game tie indicators over a random number of games, with positive dependence because closely matched series produce repeatedly close games.
nba.series_ot_count_model.rationale: KXNBASERIESOT settles on at least N overtime games (3+ in the sampled Finals market); at a per-game rate near 6% that is a deep-tail event whose probability is driven by series length and within-series dispersion, so multiplying an average OT rate by the number of games misprices it by a large factor.
nba.series_ot_count_model.measurement: For each game g of the series compute p_g from nba.reg_tie_pmf_model using that game's own-model margin (home/away alternation, current injuries); draw series length L from nba.series_model jointly with the per-game margins; count OT games with a beta-binomial-type overdispersion parameter rho estimated by comparing the observed variance of OT-game counts per series with the Poisson-binomial prediction over 20+ seasons of playoff series (all rounds); report P(count >= k) for each listed threshold k; as-of: market snapshot, after any completed games of the series are conditioned on.
free_sources: Basketball-Reference playoff series and box scores (period counts)
raw_data: playoff game period counts by series
nba.series_ot_count_model.why: Converts per-game tie probabilities into the 3+ overtime-game count that KXNBASERIESOT settles on.

nba.team_bench_points_model.label: Team bench-points model: non-starter minutes times bench scoring rate, conditional on margin path and confirmed starters
nba.team_bench_points_model.mechanism: A team's bench points equal the minutes played by non-starters times their points per minute; bench minutes rise sharply in blowouts (for both teams) and when starters exit, and the confirmed starting five decides who is counted as bench.
nba.team_bench_points_model.rationale: A bench-points quantity moves opposite to star ladders: a blowout or a starter's early exit increases bench minutes, while a pregame scratch of a starter promotes a reserve into the starting five and removes his points from the bench total. Neither the individual points inputs nor team-total inputs say who is classified as bench, which is fixed only at the starting-lineup announcement. ENTITY UNRESOLVED: for KXNBABENCHPTS (title 'NBA Bench Points', scope 'Bench Points', no market ever listed, terms file BASKETBALLENTITYSTAT.pdf which is also the terms file of player-prop series such as KXNBAPTS) it is not known whether the contract is a team's bench total, a named player's points as a bench player, or another bench unit; this input defines the team-total reading (the KXNBAH2HBENCHPTS head-to-head is a team comparison by its sampled rules), and a player-level reading would instead use the player points inputs with nba.starters_pit.
nba.team_bench_points_model.measurement: Step 1: expected bench minutes = 240 (+25 per overtime period) minus the sum of projected starter minutes, with starter minutes from nba.minutes conditioned on the margin-path curve of nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve and on confirmed starters (nba.starters_pit). Step 2: bench points per minute = minutes-weighted sum of each projected reserve's shrunk points per minute (prior weight 300 minutes toward the role mean) times the team's opponent-adjusted offensive-rating factor. Step 3: distribution by simulation over margin paths and starter-exit scenarios (foul-out, injury) with player-level negative-binomial points; calibrate dispersion on 3 seasons of team bench points from box scores with the starter flag. As-of: lineup confirmation (about 30 minutes before tip); earlier, a mixture over probable starting fives.
free_sources: nba_api boxscoretraditional (starter position flag) and leaguegamelog (free, undocumented, rate-limited)
Basketball-Reference box scores (starters listed first; free, polite scraping)
raw_data: player-game box score with starter flag, minutes and points
nba.team_bench_points_model.why: Models a team's non-starter points total for KXNBABENCHPTS (entity unresolved: team total assumed) and for the KXNBAH2HBENCHPTS difference, composing the minutes component (nba.bench_minutes_distribution), the rate component (nba.bench_scoring) and the starter definition (nba.starter_bench_definition_ledger) rather than duplicating them.

nba.ot_model.reason: Catalog measurement is an empirical P(OT) by |spread| and total bucket, i.e. keyed on market lines; the own-model nba.reg_tie_pmf_model (P(OT)) and nba.ot_period_distribution (what OT adds) replace it, and the bucketed frequency is kept only as a calibration benchmark.

nba.score_resid.reason: Catalog definition is 'Score residual distribution around lines' (actual margin/total minus the closing line, by spread bucket), a market-centred quantity; it is a benchmark only, and the own-model margin density (nba.reg_tie_pmf_model) replaces it in the stages.

nba.garbage.reason: Catalog definition is 'Blowout / garbage-time probability from spread' (measurement: P(final |margin| > 15/20/25) as a function of the closing spread), so as defined it is market-derived and only a calibration benchmark; the blowout-minutes mechanism is carried by the market-free nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve (ratings-implied margin plus coach minutes-versus-margin curve).

nba.bench_scoring.reason: Bench points per minute and depth is the second factor of the bench target, but without bench minutes it explains little.

nba.starters_pit.reason: Defines who counts as bench; essential, but the timing of confirmation and the promoted-player effect must be explicit.

nba.rotation.reason: Substitution patterns by margin decide bench minutes; needs per-coach estimates and margin-conditional minute curves.

nba.pace.reason: Pace scales sd of margin (tie mass) and team-stat counts; it is a main driver for the pair model but minor for bench minutes.

nba.q_scoring.reason: Quarter/half scoring patterns pertain to period markets, which are not in this archetype; no OT, bench or team-stat target uses them.

nba.late_game_script.reason: Relevant to the excess tie mass but too generic; the coach-level tie-forcing rate and foul-up-3 policy are needed to make it measurable.

nba.injuries_pit.reason: Starter absences set both the margin mean and the bench composition; vintage matters because replacements are only known near tip.

nba.off_rtg.reason: Draft rationale mentions race-to markets that are not in this archetype; ratings matter only to set the mean margin and scoring volumes.

nba.def_rtg.reason: Same issue as off_rtg: the rationale refers to race-to markets; defence determines mean margin only and affects tie mass weakly.

nba.three_pt_luck.reason: Claimed to drive OT frequency, but shooting luck is unpredictable and does not forecast ties; it is useful only for team three-point head-to-heads.

m.quote_history.reason: Kalshi price path for the overtime and team-event markets; useful to see when information was absorbed and for calibration labels, but it is an observation of the market, never an explanatory driver of the outcome.

m.rules_text.reason: Versioned rules text defines the settled quantity for the overtime and team-event markets; wording changes between series are the only way to know the target variable, so it is a required contract input, not a feature.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook price for the overtime and team-event markets is a market-derived quantity; keep as a comparison benchmark to measure disagreement, do not use as an input to the probability model.

m.fees.reason: Fee schedule converts a probability gap into net edge for the overtime and team-event markets; needed for decision thresholds only, constant with respect to the outcome.

nba.market_calibration_bias.reason: Reliability curves measured on Kalshi prices against de-vigged book lines are a market-derived correction layer, not a driver of whether regulation ends tied; usable only after a model probability exists, as in the sibling records.

interactions.mechanism: The tie probability is the Gaussian pmf at zero, which decays like exp(-mu^2/(2 sigma^2)); the loss from a 4-point expected margin to a 10-point expected margin is far larger than from 0 to 4, so the effect of expected margin on P(OT) is convex-then-flat in the tail.
interactions.how_to_test: Bin games by own-model expected margin (0-2, 2-5, 5-8, 8-12, 12+) and compare the observed OT rate with the Gaussian prediction and with a flat rate.

interactions.mechanism: The excess tie mass is conditional on the game being within three points with under 30 seconds left and on the trailing coach's policy; if the leading team intentionally fouls, ties become less likely than by smooth density.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate P(tie | within 3 at 0:30) by coach pair and contrast with fouling versus non-fouling policies.

interactions.mechanism: When the top scorer is promoted into the starting five by an absence, he leaves the bench count and bench points drop by his share; when a returning star plays off the bench on a restriction, bench points rise by his minutes times his rate, a discrete jump.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare bench points in games with promoted-starter and with star-off-bench changes versus baselines.

interactions.mechanism: Bench minutes rise with blowout probability but saturate once starters sit entirely, around 150-170 minutes; beyond that extra blowout size adds nothing, while within the competitive range additional margin adds quickly.
interactions.how_to_test: Plot bench minutes against final margin to find the saturation; fit a piecewise-linear spline.

interactions.mechanism: The two teams' counts rise and fall together with pace, so a pace shock moves both and leaves the difference nearly unchanged; the difference's sd is smaller than independent counts would give, and the covariance is higher in games with competitive scores.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate rho of team threes by pace tercile and by closeness of final score.

interactions.mechanism: The trailing team raises its three-point attempt share late in lopsided games while the leader slows down, so the expected made-threes difference shrinks toward zero (or flips) in blowout scripts even when the favourite is the higher-volume team; this cuts the favourite's edge in KXNBAH2HTEAM3PT.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress the fourth-quarter team 3PA share difference on the projected margin bucket and compare the H2H threes outcome rate by margin bucket against the volume-only prediction.

interactions.mechanism: A team's bench total jumps once the margin passes the coach's pull threshold early in the fourth quarter, because the starters' remaining minutes convert to reserve minutes for both sides, and a pregame starter scratch moves one reserve out of the bench pool; the level and the variance of KXNBABENCHPTS therefore switch between a normal-rotation regime and a blowout regime, and a scratch shifts the whole distribution rather than its tail.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute team bench points and bench minutes by pre-game margin-curve decile and by starter-scratch flag from box scores with the starter flag, then compare the fitted mean and sd of bench points between the two regimes.

nonlinearities.shape: Gaussian bell in the expected margin with an empirical multiplicative excess
nonlinearities.why: P(OT) falls as exp(-(expected margin/sigma)^2/2), so it declines by about 30% at a 10-point expected margin, and the excess factor lifts all levels by about 1.7-1.9.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise: flat in close games, rising then saturating in blowouts
nonlinearities.why: Bench minutes are about 90-100 when close, grow rapidly when margin exceeds 15, and cap near the whole-bench total once starters sit.

nonlinearities.shape: Geometric decay in number of OT periods
nonlinearities.why: Each extra overtime period occurs with a small probability that is roughly constant, so tail periods add little mass and multi-OT strike markets are rare events with unstable estimates.

nonlinearities.shape: convex tail in per-game tie probability and dispersion
nonlinearities.why: P(3+ OT games in a series) scales roughly with the cube of the per-game OT rate and rises sharply with within-series dependence, so a 20% error in the per-game rate becomes roughly a 70% error in the 3+ tail.

contract.settlement_definition: The sampled full-game total (KXNBATOTAL) settles Yes if the combined points in the named game exceed a half-point strike (floor_strike 274.5 for 'over 274.5 total points'), so no push is possible; the secondary text settles on the official final result for a game that starts within 48 hours of schedule and resolves to a fair price if the game is cancelled or not started within 48 hours. The wording says 'total points are scored in the ... game' without carving out overtime, so overtime is counted by default but is not explicitly stated. KXNBATOTAL is the only live series under this key.

rules_evidence.quote: If over 274.5 total points are scored in the Washington vs Atlanta Pro Basketball game originally scheduled for Nov 6, 2026
rules_evidence.establishes: Strike is a half-point 'over' on combined team points in one named game, so the target is a continuous-looking integer sum with no push.

rules_evidence.quote: If the game is postponed but begins within 48 hours of its originally scheduled start time
rules_evidence.establishes: A short postponement does not void the market: it resolves on the official final result, whereas a longer delay or cancellation resolves to fair price (void-like), so postponement risk is not a loss.

variants_and_edge_cases: Single live variant: the regular-season and playoff full-game combined points total (KXNBATOTAL); no Summer League or series-length total is filed here.

Overtime: the rule text says 'total points are scored in the ... game'; a game with one overtime adds about 24 points, so P(over) near the line rises materially when OT is included; inclusion is plausible but not stated.
Strike spacing: rungs are half-point lines, and the ladder is a survival function of a discrete integer sum, so adjacent rungs differ by P(total = k).
Postponement and cancellation: a cancelled or non-started game resolves to fair price rather than No, which affects only edge accounting.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official final score of the game (league box score), including overtime unless the full rule text excludes it.

mechanism.summary: A game total is points = possessions times combined points per possession, so the process has two multiplicative factors and one additive tail. Possessions come from the interaction of two teams' preferred tempos (pace is neither the average nor the slower team's pace, it depends on transition frequency, turnovers and who pushes after makes or misses), reduced by dead-ball time from fouls and free throws. Points per possession depend on each offence against the other's defence for the actual rotation, including who is out (a missing ball handler slows pace and lowers efficiency, a missing rim protector raises efficiency without changing pace), plus free-throw volume driven by foul rates and the officials. Three-point shooting variance is the dominant noise source so the game-level sd of about 17-19 points is heteroscedastic: higher for teams that attempt many threes. Close games add late-game fouling free throws, blowouts shorten starters' minutes, and overtime adds about 24 points in about 6% of games. The settled event is one integer sum against a half-point strike.

stages.name: Possession count from two tempos
stages.description: Game possessions are not the average of the teams' season paces; they depend on offensive transition rate, turnover and steal rates, missed-shot rebound speed and the opponent's own tempo response, plus dead-ball events (fouls, timeouts). A slow, half-court team can slow a fast opponent, but evidence that the slower team fully controls pace is mixed, so the composition rule must be estimated rather than assumed. Pace has a game-to-game sd of about 3 possessions.
stages.distribution: Approximately normal with sd of 3-4 possessions around the composed mean, with weak dependence on the game state (garbage time slightly slower or faster depending on bench).

stages.name: Active-set efficiency of both offences
stages.description: Each offence's points per possession depends on shot quality against the specific defence and on who plays; absences affect pace and efficiency differently by role (a lead ball handler out lowers assist-generated shots and pace, a rim protector out raises the opponent's rim efficiency). The relevant baseline is opponent-adjusted offence and defence separately, not net rating, because a total depends on the sum of both teams' offences rather than their difference.
stages.distribution: Normal with sd about 1.5-2.5 points per 100 possessions around the estimated rating; scenario mixture when key players are questionable.

stages.name: Shot-making noise and its volume dependence
stages.description: Game-level variance is dominated by three-point makes: each three has Bernoulli variance 9p(1-p), so a team taking 45 threes contributes much more variance than one taking 25, and the variance of the total rises with both teams' 3PA. Hot shooting regresses to talent and shot quality, so recent results must be shrunk, and the shrinkage is stronger for defences' opponent 3P%.
stages.distribution: Sum of Bernoulli/binomial shot outcomes: total sd roughly sqrt(var of 2s + var of 3s + var of FT) of about 14, plus possession and rating uncertainty giving 17-19; heteroscedastic in 3PA.

stages.name: Free-throw volume and late-game structure
stages.description: Free throws add points through foul rates (offensive drive rate, defensive contact), the officiating crew's whistle tendency and late-game fouling in close games. When the margin is within about 8 points in the last two minutes, the trailing team fouls and total points rise by 4-10; in blowouts the late phase has no intentional fouls and benches play, which reduces scoring pace for some teams and increases it for others.
stages.distribution: Right-skewed in close games (extra FT tail), compressed in blowouts; crew effect about +/-3 points in total at the extremes.

stages.name: Overtime block added to the total
stages.description: Regulation ends tied with a probability that falls as the own-model expected margin grows (nba.reg_tie_pmf_model), and each overtime period then adds a block of combined points (recalled mean about 20-24, sd about 8) with a small chance of further periods (nba.ot_period_distribution). Because the block is added on top of a near-median regulation total, a strict over near the line gains a few percentage points from OT, more in close, slow games where the tie probability is highest; a total line far from the median barely moves.
stages.distribution: Mixture: regulation total with weight 1 - P(OT), plus a right-shifted component (one or more 5-minute blocks) with weight P(OT); the OT component is lumpy because periods are discrete.
