nba.game_pace_composition.label: Game-pace composition rule from two teams' tempos
nba.game_pace_composition.mechanism: Expected game possessions as a function of both teams' pace, transition frequency and turnover rates rather than a simple average.
nba.game_pace_composition.rationale: The draft states that the slower team controls tempo; the empirical rule must be fitted, with transition frequency and defence-forced turnovers as additional terms.
nba.game_pace_composition.measurement: Regress game possessions on (paceA + paceB)/2, |paceA - paceB|, each team's transition-frequency and turnover rate and rest, using 5 seasons of team-games with opponent-adjusted paces (20-game half-life); report coefficients and residual sd; as-of the last completed game; adjust for active set via nba.absence_pace_efficiency_decomposition.
nba.game_pace_composition.why: Total is multiplicative in possessions, so a 2-possession error shifts the mean total by about 4 points.

nba.absence_pace_efficiency_decompositio.label: Absence effect split into pace and efficiency components
nba.absence_pace_efficiency_decompositio.mechanism: Each rotation player's absence changes team pace and ORtg/DRtg separately, with different signs by role.
nba.absence_pace_efficiency_decompositio.rationale: The existing lineup_adj_rating collapses availability into one net rating, which is the right variable for margin but wrong for totals where a slower-and-worse offence and a faster-and-weaker defence have opposite effects.
nba.absence_pace_efficiency_decompositio.measurement: For each player with at least 800 minutes: on/off differences in team possessions per 48, ORtg and DRtg over 3 seasons with ridge shrinkage (k=600 possessions) and teammate adjustment (RAPM-style regression on pace as well); apply to tonight's scenario weights; as-of nightly after injury report.
raw_data: Lineup stints (five-man on-court sets) with start/end clock, possessions, points for and against
Injury-report status per player at as-of time
nba.absence_pace_efficiency_decompositio.why: The draft's interaction about ball handlers and rim protectors has no measurable input behind it.

nba.three_point_variance_load.label: Three-point attempt volume as a variance load
nba.three_point_variance_load.mechanism: The sd of the total depends on how many threes both teams attempt and on the dispersion of free-throw and two-point results.
nba.three_point_variance_load.rationale: The draft says total sd is about 17-19 as a constant; it varies with shot mix, and wide-open three-heavy teams produce a wider total distribution that matters at ladder tails.
nba.three_point_variance_load.measurement: Var(total) = Var(possessions) x ppp^2 + sum over both teams of E[3PA] x 9 x p3(1-p3) + E[2PA] x 4 x p2(1-p2) + E[FTA] x pft(1-pft) x (1 + dispersion), plus the covariance 2 x Cov(possessions, ppp) x E[poss] x ppp, using opponent-adjusted attempts and rates (20-game half-life) as of tipoff; Var(possessions) estimated from 3 seasons of team-game pace residuals. Calibrate a scalar lambda so that predicted variance divided by realised squared residual of total points in the 2 previous seasons equals 1 (rolling), report sd per game and skew from the third moment of the same components. All inputs are team shot counts, not lines. As-of: games before tip.
nba.three_point_variance_load.why: Ladder rungs far from the mean depend on the tail; using a constant sd misprices those rungs.

nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.label: Own-model regulation tie probability P(OT)
nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.mechanism: P(OT) = mass of regulation margin at zero from a heteroscedastic margin density with a late-game excess-mass correction.
nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.rationale: The draft claims P(OT) is roughly flat across spreads, but a Gaussian with sd 12 gives 3.3% at pick-em and 2.3% at 10 points, so the dependence on spread is large; the right model is a decreasing function with an empirical excess factor.
nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.measurement: P_gauss(0) = phi(mu/sigma)/sigma with mu own-model margin and sigma from own ratings and pace (nba.lineup_adj_rating and nba.pace; about 12, scaling with sqrt(possessions)); multiply by excess factor kappa(|mu|) estimated by isotonic regression on 10 seasons of games as observed OT rate divided by P_gauss(0) in |mu| buckets of 2 points; kappa about 1.7-1.9 overall; output with beta interval; use own-model mu, not closing lines. Margin is integer-valued with parity tied to the total, and free-throw, three-point and intentional-foul structure moves mass onto and off zero, so estimate the observed integer pmf at 0 (and smoothed mass at +/-1 to +/-4) over 15 seasons and let kappa(|mu|) absorb the discreteness rather than reading the continuous density at zero.
nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.why: Market-free probability that regulation ends tied, from the own-model margin mean and sd with an integer-pmf excess at zero; needed because overtime changes the settled quantity.
raw_data: team-game regulation and final scores with period counts (15 seasons)
own-model expected margin and sd per game

nba.ot_period_distribution.label: Distribution of number of overtime periods and OT scoring
nba.ot_period_distribution.mechanism: If overtime occurs, additional periods occur with a small probability and each period adds a fixed block of minutes and points.
nba.ot_period_distribution.rationale: The count of OT periods matters for series OT markets and for strike markets on total, bench or team stats within the family; the draft treats OT as one event.
nba.ot_period_distribution.measurement: Empirical P(k OT periods) from 15 seasons: P(1), P(2), P(3+) conditional on OT; per-period points per team sampled from the league distribution adjusted for pace (mean about 11-12 per team per 5 minutes, sd 5); update yearly; for series OT: P(at least one OT game) = sum over series length L of P(L) * (1 - prod over games g of (1 - p_g)), with P(L) from nba.series_model (4-7 games, shorter for mismatched teams) and p_g from nba.reg_tie_pmf_model using each game's own-model margin; inflate the variance across games because closeness is positively correlated within a series (estimate by the observed share of series with >=1 OT game versus the independent prediction on 15 seasons of playoff series). The settled quantity (at least one OT game, or a count) is unsampled, see u6.
nba.ot_period_distribution.why: An overtime period adds roughly a 10-12 point block per team to the total and a second OT adds another, so the OT-count distribution shapes the upper tail of the total.
raw_data: Game period counts and OT scores

nba.pace.reason: Possessions are the first multiplicative factor; the entry measures each team's pace but not the two-team composition rule that decides game pace.

nba.off_rtg.reason: For totals offence matters separately from defence; opponent adjustment and shot-luck regression are required.

nba.def_rtg.reason: Defence sets opponent scoring; the draft's remark on shot-luck adjustment is right because opponent 3P% is largely luck.

nba.lineup_adj_rating.reason: It is a net rating (offence minus defence), whereas a total depends on the sum of offences, so net rating confounds a good-offence-bad-defence team with a balanced one.

nba.injuries_pit.reason: Report vintage matters, and the role of the missing player (scorer, ball handler, rim protector) decides the sign on the total.

nba.three_pt_luck.reason: Regresses hot three-point shooting, a direct driver of recent totals; effect proportional to 3PA volume.

nba.fouls_ft.reason: Team foul-drawing and free-throw rate for both sides; kept secondary and scoped to the team-level rate only so it does not double count nba.referee_crew (official-level whistle shift after controlling for team rates) or nba.late_game_script (closeness-conditional intentional fouling).

nba.referee_crew.reason: A credible total driver (whistle tendency) but the effect is concentrated in high-FTA games and needs the crew assignment known on game day.

nba.rest_travel.reason: Rest affects efficiency and slightly pace; effect on totals is small compared with ratings and pace.

nba.travel_altitude.reason: The rest_travel definition already lists altitude and travel; listing altitude again repeats the same schedule-environment source.

nba.late_game_script.reason: Intentional fouling in close games adds points to the total; needs an explicit closeness-conditional free-throw point term.

nba.ot_model.reason: Catalog measurement is an empirical P(OT) by |spread| bucket and total bucket, keyed on market lines, so it is a benchmark; the own-model nba.reg_tie_pmf_model supplies P(OT) and nba.ot_period_distribution the points an overtime adds.

nba.score_resid.reason: Total residual 'around lines' is market-centred; the sd should come from own-model volume (nba.three_point_variance_load) rather than a constant of 17-19.

nba.standings_motivation.reason: Relevant mainly through who plays in late-season games; low incremental value if availability inputs are good.

nba.def_scheme.reason: Scheme interacts with shot profile to change points per possession at equal ratings; weak evidence in the regular season.

nba.shot_profile.reason: Three-heavy offences against drop coverages gain; also feeds the variance load.

m.quote_history.reason: Kalshi price path for the full-game total ladder; useful to see when information was absorbed and for calibration labels, but it is an observation of the market, never an explanatory driver of the outcome.

m.rules_text.reason: Versioned rules text defines the settled quantity for the full-game total ladder; wording changes between series are the only way to know the target variable, so it is a required contract input, not a feature.

m.external_lines.reason: The sharp total is the efficient benchmark for the mean; useful for measuring disagreement, not as a model input.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Cross-rung monotonicity of the full-game total ladder is derived from Kalshi prices, so it flags stale quotes (an execution diagnostic) and carries no information about the underlying result.

m.orderbook_depth.reason: Depth and spread on the full-game total ladder set tradable size and minimum edge; they come from the market itself and say nothing about the event mechanism.

nba.market_calibration_bias.reason: Price-bucket miscalibration for the full-game total ladder is measured on Kalshi prices, so it is a market-derived correction layer applied after a probability exists, not an input.

m.volume_oi.reason: Volume/open interest for the full-game total ladder measures liquidity and attention; market-derived and not a driver of the outcome, usable only to discount thin quotes.

m.trade_tape.reason: Trade prints for the full-game total ladder are market microstructure; informed-flow inference from them is speculative and cannot be a causal input.

m.settlement_truth.reason: Settled value and timestamp for the full-game total ladder are labels for calibration and need reconciling against the named source; not a pregame input.

nba.series_model.reason: Attached earlier for KXNBASERIESGAMES and series-total wording; both left this key, and the sole live series KXNBATOTAL is one game, so the best-of-seven model generates nothing settled here.

nba.summer_league_minutes.reason: Attached earlier for KXNBASUMMERTOTAL, which moved to summer_league_games; KXNBATOTAL covers regular-season and playoff games only, so Summer League minutes plans are not an input of this key.

interactions.mechanism: Total equals possessions times combined points per possession, so a fast game between two efficient offences is multiplicatively larger than the sum of separate pace and efficiency effects; the cross term is about 1.5-2 points when both factors are one sd above average.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress total on pace, efficiency and the pace-by-efficiency product across 5 seasons and test the product term.

interactions.mechanism: Missing a primary ball handler lowers pace and efficiency (total falls), while missing a rim protector raises opponent efficiency without changing pace (total rises); the sign depends on the missing role.
interactions.how_to_test: Group games by missing player role and compare residual totals; verify opposite signs.

interactions.mechanism: Crew whistle tendency matters most for teams that live at the line: a high-foul crew adds free-throw points proportional to both teams' free-throw rate, so the crew effect on total is larger when both offences draw many fouls.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact crew foul index with the sum of both teams' FTA rate and test the slope.

interactions.mechanism: A hot three-point streak is more likely to be luck for a high-3PA team (larger noise per game), so regression is heavier for those teams and the variance load is also larger; direction: shrink recent offence more when volume is high.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress next-game total residual on last-10 3P% residual interacted with 3PA rate.

interactions.mechanism: Close games produce both late-fouling free-throw points and OT, so the extra points are positively correlated within the same games; the upper tail of the total is generated by close games more than by high-pace blowouts.
interactions.how_to_test: Condition total residuals on final margin buckets and compare tail mass of high rungs in close vs non-close games.

nonlinearities.shape: Variance increasing in 3PA, sd scales with sqrt(attempts)
nonlinearities.why: The sd of the total rises with the number of threes (9p(1-p) per attempt), so rung probabilities away from the mean are sensitive to shot mix.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold at margin within about 8 points in the last 2 minutes
nonlinearities.why: Intentional fouling begins when a game is within a possession or two; adds 4-10 points only in that state, a switch rather than a slope in the margin.

nonlinearities.shape: Mixture adding a fixed block to the upper tail
nonlinearities.why: The regulation total plus a 24-point OT block in 6% of games creates a bump to the right of the median that a normal misses.

nonlinearities.shape: Sub-linear in the slower team's pace
nonlinearities.why: If the slow team partially controls tempo, game pace responds less than one-for-one to the faster team's tempo, so the average of paces overstates the effect of the fast side.
