contract.settlement_definition: Three live series, all with recovered rules text. KXNBAPREPACK2ML and KXNBAPREPACK3ML are pre-packaged multi-game moneyline combos: Yes only if every named team wins its named game (sampled: two or three different Christmas Day 2025 games, each identified by its original schedule date). Their text has no secondary clause, so postponement, cancellation or a voided leg is not addressed. KXNBANHL is a cross-league championship pair: Yes if the named NBA team wins the 2026-27 NBA title and the named NHL team wins the 2026-27 Stanley Cup, and No as soon as either team is eliminated. No same-game player/team parlay series is live; stages s1-s5 describe that mechanism for completeness and do not serve a live series.

rules_evidence.quote: must win the championship in the 2026-27 Pro Basketball and NHL seasons
rules_evidence.establishes: The only live combination is a two-leg cross-league futures pair: Yes needs both named teams to win their league titles in the same season.

rules_evidence.quote: If one of the teams is eliminated from championship contention in the 2026-27 Pro Basketball and NHL seasons, then the market resolves to No.
rules_evidence.establishes: The combo resolves No at the first elimination of either leg, so it is a path-dependent knockout whose value collapses as soon as one team is out.

rules_evidence.quote: If Minnesota wins against Denver, Los Angeles L wins against Houston in Minnesota at Denver professional basketball game originally scheduled for Dec 25, 2025
rules_evidence.establishes: The 2-leg pack needs both named teams to win their own separate games on the same slate; legs are in different games, so the joint is close to a product of game win probabilities.

rules_evidence.quote: San Antonio wins against Oklahoma City, Golden State wins against Dallas, Los Angeles L wins against Houston
rules_evidence.establishes: The 3-leg pack is the same all-legs-win construction over three different games, so small errors in each leg's win probability compound multiplicatively.

variants_and_edge_cases: Cross-league futures pair (KXNBANHL): two independent title races resolve within the same spring; the early-No clause means the contract can settle months before the second title is decided, and there are no void legs.

Void-leg treatment: the live pack texts have no postponement or cancellation clause, so whether a pack voids, drops the leg or resolves No when one game is postponed is not stated (u1); single-leg game markets use a 48-hour rule and fair-price void.

Cross-game versus same-game combos: the live packs (KXNBAPREPACK2ML/3ML) put legs in different games, where dependence is limited to shared information (same-day injury news, slate-wide officiating or rule effects) and is close to zero; same-game legs (not live) share margin, total, minutes and injury shocks.
Leg types mix half-point lines (no push) and integer N+ player thresholds (no push), but a whole-number sportsbook-style line could create a push leg whose handling inside a parlay is unseen.
Protected player legs (first-half-exit void) add a conditional-on-survival structure that interacts with other legs through the injury event.
Payoff is the product of marginals only under independence; pricing by the market maker embeds an assumed correlation that may differ from the true one.

Nested and logically implied legs: a spread cover implies the moneyline win, an N+ leg implies every lower N+ leg for the same player, and a PRA leg is a sum of its component legs, so such combinations have degenerate or perfect dependence that a Gaussian copula over marginals cannot represent; leg-count limits and whether nested legs are allowed are unknown.
Moneyline legs include overtime implicitly (NBA games cannot tie), so each pack leg is a plain win indicator with no push.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official final results of each named game (packs); official NBA Finals and Stanley Cup Final results and elimination events (KXNBANHL).

mechanism.summary: A multi-leg combination resolves true only when all legs hold, so the probability is the joint probability of a vector of events, and the information needed is the dependence structure, not just the leg marginals. Same-game legs share latent factors: the margin (favourite covering moves the starters' minutes), the pace/total (more possessions raise all counting stats), team shooting luck (a hot night lifts all of a team's scorers together), and the injury/availability shock (one news item moves many legs). Within a team the allocation of points among players is a zero-sum split of a fixed team total, so two teammates' point overs are negatively associated at a given team score but positively associated through the team total. The joint is therefore best produced by a game-level simulation with explicit factors, not by pairwise correlations, and calibrated on historical box scores. Product-of-marginals pricing is biased: positive dependence makes joint hits more likely, negative makes them less likely, and the direction flips with leg type and team side. Three combinations are live and none is same-game: KXNBAPREPACK2ML/3ML are multi-game moneyline packs whose legs are separate games, so their probability is essentially the product of per-game win probabilities computed on one consistent information set, and KXNBANHL is a cross-league futures pair that is a product of two title probabilities with path-dependent early-No settlement. The same-game machinery (s1-s5) is retained for completeness but serves no live series.

stages.name: Leg marginals from their own mechanisms
stages.description: Each leg has its own generating process (a spread cover from the margin density, a total from pace and efficiency, a player stat from minutes and rates), and the joint can only be as good as these marginals. The marginals must be computed on the same information set and the same scenario weights for injuries, otherwise the dependence is applied to inconsistent inputs.
stages.distribution: Each marginal is a Bernoulli with probabilities from 0.05 to 0.95; leg probabilities combine multiplicatively under independence, which is the baseline to test against.

stages.name: Shared game-level latent factors
stages.description: Same-game legs load on a handful of common factors: the game total (pace times efficiency) moves every player's counting stats in the same direction; the margin moves starters' minutes and shot attempts together in favourites' blowouts; team-specific shooting luck lifts the team's scorers jointly. A factor model estimated on historical box scores gives the loadings by leg type and player role, and these loadings are what a simulation needs.
stages.distribution: Gaussian-like factor shocks with factor correlation near zero between margin and total (about 0.0-0.1) but strongly positive between total and any player points (loadings of 0.3-0.6).

stages.name: Minutes and blowout linkage
stages.description: The favourite-cover leg and a star-over leg are tied through minutes: a blowout lets the favourite cover but removes starters' late minutes on both sides, because the trailing coach also pulls starters. The minutes link is therefore a function of |expected margin| and is negative for both teams' stars against a favourite-cover leg; only the usage and score-state effect is side-specific (the trailing team's stars shoot more until pulled, the leader's share falls). The strength is a threshold in |expected margin|, not a constant: it appears only when the expected margin is large enough for starters to sit, and it is stronger for older stars and for coaches who pull early.
stages.distribution: Piecewise: near zero for expected margins below about 6, increasing in magnitude beyond for the minutes component (symmetric across sides); the usage component is side-specific and smaller. Sizes are recalled (u6).

stages.name: Within-team allocation and common shocks
stages.description: Given team points, individual points are a split, so overs on two teammates are negatively dependent conditional on the team total, while a single availability shock (a star ruled out) moves many legs at once and in different directions (the star's legs fail; teammates' usage legs rise). A game-level simulation that draws the injury scenario first, then team factors, then allocation preserves these dependencies.
stages.distribution: Dirichlet-multinomial-like allocation with negative within-team dependence of about -0.1 to -0.3; discrete scenario mixture for availability.

stages.name: Joint evaluation and void-leg settlement
stages.description: The final stage evaluates the joint probability from the simulation and applies the settlement rules for combos: if any leg can void (inactive player, protected exit, postponement), the payoff must be conditioned on the combination's rule, which changes the effective probability. Sampling error in the simulation and uncertainty in dependence parameters give interval estimates, not points, for the joint. Nested or implied legs are handled by evaluating every leg on the same simulated game draws (so implication holds exactly) rather than through a copula over marginals; whether such combinations may be listed is unknown (u5).
stages.distribution: Monte Carlo estimate with standard error sqrt(p(1-p)/n): about 0.5 percentage points at p = 0.5 and 10,000 draws, but only about 0.17 points (6% relative) at p = 3% and 0.07 points (14% relative) at p = 0.5%, so small joint probabilities need importance sampling or many more draws; dependence-parameter uncertainty adds comparable error.

stages.name: Cross-league title pair (live KXNBANHL)
stages.description: The live combo pays only if the named NBA team wins the title and the named NHL team wins the Stanley Cup. The NBA leg is a bracket simulation over seeds, series win probabilities and star health; the NHL leg comes from the NHL title model, which this NBA catalog does not own. Because the two leagues share no games, players or officials, the joint is the product of the two probabilities, and the early-No clause makes the price fall to zero at the first elimination of either team, so the path of both playoff runs (overlapping in April-June) and not only the end state matters for when the contract settles.
stages.distribution: Product of two small title probabilities (often 1-10% each, so the joint is usually below 1%); path-dependent with absorbing No states at each elimination round in either league.

stages.name: Multi-game moneyline packs (live KXNBAPREPACK2ML/3ML)
stages.description: Each pack leg is the named team winning its own game, so the joint is the product of per-game win probabilities, each built from availability-adjusted team ratings, home court and rest for that game. Because the games share no players, the only dependence is common information timing (late injury news on the same slate) and shared slate conditions, which are small; the main error source is compounding: three legs at 0.60 give 0.216, and a 0.03 error per leg moves the product by about 0.03 (15% relative). Leg probabilities must come from the own game model, not from listed moneylines.
stages.distribution: Product of 2-3 near-independent Bernoullis with leg probabilities 0.2-0.9; relative error grows with leg count; joint usually 0.05-0.5.

talent_strength.note: Leg marginals inherit talent from the single-leg mechanisms.

opponent_matchup.note: Matchup effects live inside each leg's marginal (opponent-adjusted rates for players, opponent defence for totals); the combination layer adds no matchup variable of its own beyond the dependence between legs.

role_personnel.note: Role determines how legs load on shared factors.

availability_news.note: A single availability item moves many legs and creates void states.

coaching_scheme.note: Pull timing creates the minutes link between margin and player legs.

environment.note: Venue, altitude and weather enter through each leg's own marginal; the combination layer has no environmental variable of its own beyond pace in the shared factors.

game_context_script.note: Blowout script links margin to minutes.

pace_volume.note: Pace and team totals as shared factors.

efficiency_conversion.note: Shooting efficiency is part of each leg's marginal; the correlated team shooting luck factor is carried by nba.game_factor_loadings, so no separate efficiency input is needed at the combo layer.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest, back-to-back and late-season incentives change minutes for several legs simultaneously, but no combo-level input quantifies a rest-driven common shock; only each leg's own treatment exists.

officiating_rules.note: Crew tendencies affect foul and free-throw counts in individual legs; the combination layer inherits this through marginals, and no separate officiating variable is warranted for dependence.

settlement_contract.note: All three live series have rules text: multi-game moneyline packs (all named teams win their separate games; no void clause) and the cross-league title pair with early No. Same-game parlay rules do not exist (no series).

nba.game_factor_loadings.label: Game-level latent factor loadings by leg type
nba.game_factor_loadings.mechanism: Legs load on shared factors (pace/total, margin, team shooting luck, availability) with loadings that differ by leg type and player role.
nba.game_factor_loadings.rationale: The draft lists covariance of a single player's stats, but multi-leg dependence spans legs from different mechanisms; a factor model captures it with a manageable parameter count.
nba.game_factor_loadings.measurement: Build leg indicators without any line: team margin above own-model expectation (nba.own_model_team_totals), game total above own-model total, and player stat above the own-model mean at typical thresholds. Transform each indicator to normal scores through its marginal CDF (probability integral transform on own-model predictive distribution) over 6 seasons; fit a 3-factor (total, margin, team luck) Gaussian factor model with loadings per team-side and role cell (starter guard, wing, big) by ridge-penalised maximum likelihood on the latent scale (tetrachoric correlations for binary legs). Report loadings and their sd over 100 bootstrap draws of games; as-of end of previous game.
nba.game_factor_loadings.why: Same-game dependence cannot be estimated pair by pair given the thin sample per player; a factor structure gives usable estimates.

nba.within_team_allocation_dependence.label: Within-team scoring allocation dependence
nba.within_team_allocation_dependence.mechanism: Teammates split a fixed team total, giving negative dependence between teammates' counts conditional on team points.
nba.within_team_allocation_dependence.rationale: Treating two teammates' overs as positively dependent through the team total omits the allocation effect that offsets it at fixed pace; the net sign depends on how much variation in the team total versus in the split drives each leg.
nba.within_team_allocation_dependence.measurement: For each team and pair of top-6 players, compute the correlation of player points conditional on team points (partial correlation) using 3 seasons of games, shrunk to the role-pair prior with k=40 games; combine with team total correlation to get unconditional pairwise correlations; separate regimes with/without a major teammate absence.
nba.within_team_allocation_dependence.why: Same-team parlay legs (two players' overs) are the most common correlated combination and the net sign is not obvious.

nba.leg_void_state.label: Leg void-state probabilities and combo payoff rule
nba.leg_void_state.mechanism: The combination's payoff depends on how a void leg (inactive player, protected early exit, postponement) is treated.
nba.leg_void_state.rationale: If one leg can void, the effective probability of Yes given not void differs from the product of the remaining legs, and the void probability itself is correlated with other legs through the injury event.
nba.leg_void_state.measurement: For each leg: P(void) = P(inactive) + P(protected early exit) + P(postponement beyond 48 hours) from the availability model; compute joint outcome probabilities for each void combination; apply the contract's rule (void whole, drop leg, or No) to compute the payoff probability; the rule is an input to be read from rules_primary when a combo series is live.
nba.leg_void_state.why: The combo's expected value changes in sign for a rule that drops a void leg versus one that fails it.

nba.own_model_team_totals.label: Own-model expected team points and total (market-free shared scoring factor)
nba.own_model_team_totals.mechanism: Expected team points = expected game possessions times availability-adjusted points per possession against the specific opponent, with a residual distribution built from own predictions; gives the shared scoring factor that same-game legs load on.
nba.own_model_team_totals.rationale: The shared pace/total factor must come from an own-model team total because a total implied by sportsbook lines is a market output and cannot serve as an input; this input also supplies the margin-total residual correlation that sportsbook-implied totals cannot.
nba.own_model_team_totals.measurement: possessions = pace composition of the two teams (nba.pace, lineup-aware, last 20 games weighted with half-life 8 games, shrunk to league mean with k=15 games); points per possession = availability-adjusted offence versus opponent defence rating with home adjustment, shrunk with k=20 games; team points = possessions x ppp; residual sd by team from own predictions on 5 seasons (not closing lines); output joint (margin, total) mean and covariance for the simulation.
nba.own_model_team_totals.why: Replaces the BENCHMARK_ONLY market-implied team total in the shared-factor stage so the combination does not inherit the book's prices.

nba.minutes_scenario_mixture.label: Minutes scenario mixture weights and component rates
nba.minutes_scenario_mixture.mechanism: Minutes are a mixture of regimes (blowout truncation, normal, foul-limited, OT, restricted) whose weights depend on game state and each regime has different per-minute stat rates.
nba.minutes_scenario_mixture.rationale: The existing nba.minutes is a point projection that hides the multimodality; for a threshold sum, P(S>=25) is driven by the weight of the full-minutes regime, not by the mean minutes.
nba.minutes_scenario_mixture.measurement: From 3+ seasons of play-by-play, classify each player-game into regimes by the minutes and score margin (blowout: |margin|>=18 with 4th-quarter minutes<8; foul-limited: >=4 fouls by Q3; OT; restriction: coach-announced); fit regime weights as a multinomial logit of (own-model spread, rest, opponent pace, bench depth) with ridge shrinkage; each regime's stat-per-minute rates estimated with 15-game half-life and a prior from players of the same role; as-of timestamp = last injury report vintage.
nba.minutes_scenario_mixture.why: Replaces the single minutes projection: the shared driver between legs is minutes as a function of game state (blowout, foul, restriction, overtime), which is what links a cover leg to a player leg.

nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.label: Ratings-based blowout probability and starter-minutes-vs-margin curve (market-free)
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.mechanism: Rebuilds the blowout risk from team strength and rotation history instead of the closing spread: a ratings-implied expected margin and margin spread give P(large lead), and a coach/player minutes-versus-margin curve converts each margin path into expected minutes lost by starters and gained by bench players.
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.rationale: The catalog input nba.garbage is defined from the closing spread, which is a market price and so a benchmark, not an input. The causal quantity is the chance that the margin passes the coach's pull threshold early enough to matter, and how much playing time each player then loses. Subtle: the loss depends on when the lead arrives (a 20-point lead entering Q4 removes far more starter minutes than one reached with 3 minutes left), on the coach, and on whether the trailing team also pulls starters, so the curve must be conditional on the margin path and not only on the final margin.
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.measurement: Step 1, expected margin: mu = (NetRtg_home_adj - NetRtg_away_adj) * expected_possessions/100 + home_adv, where NetRtg_adj is the as-of-tipoff opponent-adjusted net rating from nba.off_rtg and nba.def_rtg (ridge regression on game point differential, half-life about 25 games, shrunk to the preseason prior with n_prior about 20 games as a placeholder to be fitted), adjusted for the confirmed unavailable players via nba.lineup_adj_rating, home_adv fitted on the last 5 seasons (about 2 points). Step 2, margin spread: sd_margin fitted on 5 seasons of residuals of final margin versus mu (league-wide roughly 12-13 points, to be estimated, with a heavier empirical tail than normal). Step 3: P(final |margin| >= 15/20/25) and P(|lead| >= 15/20 entering Q4) from the empirical residual distribution around mu. Step 4, minutes curve: from play-by-play stints, per team-season, expected minutes of each rotation player conditional on margin entering Q4 in bins (0-9, 10-14, 15-19, 20+), shrunk toward the league curve with k about 30 blowout games. Output per player: expected minutes lost and the probability of falling below a stated minutes level. No closing line or other price is used; the spread is retained only to benchmark calibration of step 3.

nba.margin_heteroscedasticity.label: Pace- and total-dependent margin standard deviation (own-model, not line-based)
nba.margin_heteroscedasticity.mechanism: Margin variance scales with possession count and total scoring, and with spread through garbage time.
nba.margin_heteroscedasticity.rationale: The existing score_resid is defined around lines, which is market-derived; the variance should come from the game's own pace/total estimates so that cover probabilities at wide spreads are correct.
nba.margin_heteroscedasticity.measurement: Fit sd_margin = a + b × sqrt(own-model possessions) + c × |own-model mean margin| on 5 seasons of team-games (own predictions, not closing lines); report quantile curves (10/25/50/75/90) with a skew parameter for heavy favourites; validate by the probability integral transform per bucket.
nba.margin_heteroscedasticity.why: Own-model margin sd by pace and total gives the margin factor's scale for cover legs without centring on market lines.
raw_data: Walk-forward own-model mean margin and possessions

nba.title_path.label: Playoff bracket path, matchup and home-court structure
nba.title_path.mechanism: Series winner and title probabilities depend on the bracket path (seed, opponent strength, home-court) and matchup-specific adjustments.
nba.title_path.rationale: Title odds are the product of series-win probabilities along a path that depends on which seed you are, who you face and the rest/injury states. A given team's path difficulty can differ substantially even for equal rating. Subtle: series outcomes are correlated through injuries to key players across rounds.
nba.title_path.measurement: Shared playoff bracket simulation for the bracket-level consumers attached to it (season_futures_team, series_and_cup, player_milestones for KXNBAPLAYOFF3D, the playoff single-game points archetype, awards_draft and parlay_combo): 50,000 draws; seeds from nba.standings_sim paths, play-in from nba.play_in_path_model, each series simulated game by game with the per-series kernel of nba.series_length_distribution (p_g from playoff ratings, 2-2-1-1-1 home court, injury state, series dependence); store per-path series lengths, venues and advancement so these consumers read the same draws. Single-series contracts whose matchup is already set (series cumulative points, per-series length markets) use the kernel directly; it equals title_path's conditional for that series. Output P(reach round r), P(title), opponents and games played per team. As-of: nightly.
nba.title_path.why: The NBA leg of the live KXNBANHL pair is the named team's title probability from a bracket simulation.

nba.cross_league_title_combo.label: Cross-league championship pair probability (NBA title x NHL Stanley Cup) with early-elimination path
nba.cross_league_title_combo.mechanism: P(Yes) = P(named NBA team wins the title) x P(named NHL team wins the Stanley Cup), with no shared games or players to create dependence; Yes is lost at the first elimination of either team.
nba.cross_league_title_combo.rationale: KXNBANHL is the only live series under this key and it is a futures pair, not a same-game parlay, so none of the same-game dependence inputs apply. The NHL probability is outside the NBA catalog and must come from the NHL model on the same as-of timestamp; the subtle parts are the path (elimination of either leg ends the contract early) and that thin, longshot-heavy pair prices are where market miscalibration is likely, which this input must not borrow from prices.
nba.cross_league_title_combo.measurement: P_NBA from nba.title_path (at least 10,000 bracket draws, as-of the quote timestamp); P_NHL from the NHL catalog at the same timestamp: seeds from nhl.season_sim_distribution, bracket from nhl.bracket_path_difficulty, each series from nhl.series_context, giving P(named NHL team wins the Stanley Cup); both legs must use snapshots taken within the same nightly run (as-of = min of the two model timestamps). Joint = P_NBA x P_NHL, independence checked on historical seasons (correlation of title indicators for same-metro NBA/NHL pairs, expected near zero). Also output P(both alive after each round) from the two round-survival curves and set the value to zero at either elimination.
raw_data: NBA title simulation output by team and round
NHL title simulation output by team and round
nba.cross_league_title_combo.why: The live KXNBANHL pair is priced from two title probabilities and the early-elimination path, which no same-game input provides.

nba.multi_game_ml_pack_model.label: Multi-game moneyline pack joint probability
nba.multi_game_ml_pack_model.mechanism: An all-legs-win pack over separate games is the product of per-game win probabilities with a small correction for shared same-slate information.
nba.multi_game_ml_pack_model.rationale: KXNBAPREPACK2ML/3ML settle Yes only if every named team wins; with legs in different games, independence is nearly right, but leg errors compound multiplicatively and late same-day injury news can hit several legs' information sets at once, so the legs must be priced on one consistent as-of snapshot.
nba.multi_game_ml_pack_model.measurement: For each leg compute P(win) from the own game model (availability-adjusted net rating difference + home court + rest, margin sd about 12, normal CDF at zero including the OT split); joint = product of leg probabilities; test residual cross-game dependence by comparing realised pack hit rates with products over 10 seasons of same-day game pairs (expect correlation near zero); propagate leg-probability uncertainty (posterior sd per leg) to an interval on the product; as-of: a single snapshot time for all legs.
nba.multi_game_ml_pack_model.why: Produces the joint probability for the live multi-game moneyline packs from own-model leg probabilities.

nba.score_resid.reason: Catalog definition is 'Score residual distribution around lines' (actual margin/total minus the closing line, by spread bucket), a market-centred quantity; it is a benchmark only, and the own-model margin density (nba.margin_heteroscedasticity with nba.game_factor_loadings and nba.own_model_team_totals) replaces it in the stages.

nba.stat_dist.reason: Player stat marginals feed every prop leg; the combination only adds value if marginals are calibrated on the same information set.

nba.combo_covariance.reason: Covariance of PRA components is within-player and applies when legs are components of one player; it does not give cross-player or cross-leg-type dependence.

nba.garbage.reason: Catalog definition is 'Blowout / garbage-time probability from spread' (measurement: P(final |margin| > 15/20/25) as a function of the closing spread), so as defined it is market-derived and only a calibration benchmark; the blowout-minutes mechanism is carried by the market-free nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve (ratings-implied margin plus coach minutes-versus-margin curve).

nba.implied_team_totals.reason: Derived from sportsbook spread and total, which are market prices; use an own-model team total for the shared factor and keep this as a benchmark.

nba.minutes.reason: The relevant object for dependence between legs is minutes as a function of game state, which nba.minutes_scenario_mixture supplies; the single projection is kept only as a summary and removed from the stage lists.

nba.injuries_pit.reason: A single report moves many legs; the status vintage is the main common shock and creates correlated repricing.

nba.pace.reason: Pace is a shared factor for totals and counting stats; its weight in the factor model should be estimated rather than assumed.

m.quote_history.reason: Kalshi price path for multi-leg combinations; useful to see when information was absorbed and for calibration labels, but it is an observation of the market, never an explanatory driver of the outcome.

m.rules_text.reason: Versioned rules text defines the settled quantity for multi-leg combinations; wording changes between series are the only way to know the target variable, so it is a required contract input, not a feature.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook same-game-parlay prices embed an unknown correlation and a large margin; usable only as a comparison, never as an input to the dependence model.

m.fees.reason: Fee schedule converts a probability gap into net edge for multi-leg combinations; needed for decision thresholds only, constant with respect to the outcome.

nba.lineup_adj_rating.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (stage s7) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

nba.rest_travel.reason: Detached-reference repair: this archetype's own record already relies on this input (stage s7) but its input list did not carry it; attached as context so the list supplies what the mechanism asserts.

interactions.mechanism: The favourite-cover and star-over pair (for stars of either team) becomes negatively dependent through minutes only when the projected |expected margin| passes about 6-8 points, since starters of both teams sit only in lopsided games; below the threshold the two are close to independent.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the correlation of cover and star-over indicators in expected margin buckets of 2 points and look for a knee.

interactions.mechanism: A single pace shock lifts the game total and every player's counting stats, so total-over with two player overs has a high joint probability beyond the product; loadings determine how much.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate with and without the pace factor and compare the joint to the product on historical games.

interactions.mechanism: When a major teammate is ruled out, allocation shifts and the previously negative dependence between two remaining teammates' overs can turn less negative because both gain usage; the sign is conditional on the injury scenario.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate partial correlations separately in games with and without the major teammate.

interactions.mechanism: The same injury news produces a void leg (player inactive) or a live leg with a minute limit; the combo rule on void legs switches the payoff structure, so the effective probability is regime-dependent.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute payoff probabilities under each void rule using historical status vintages and compare.

interactions.mechanism: The correlation between margin and total is close to zero overall but positive for slow-paced underdog games and negative for fast-paced favourite runaways, so the joint is not a simple bivariate normal.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the correlation within cells of pace and spread and test heterogeneity.

interactions.mechanism: The pair's value is the product of the two title probabilities only while both teams are alive; once the NBA leg's team advances a round the pair's value rises proportionally, and any elimination is absorbing, so value moves as a function of the round reached in both leagues.
interactions.how_to_test: Track simulated pair values by round reached in each league on past seasons and compare them with the product of the two legs' round-conditional title probabilities.

interactions.mechanism: A late scratch on one leg moves only that leg's win probability, but because the pack is a product, a drop from 0.65 to 0.50 on one leg cuts the 3-leg joint by 23% relative; status uncertainty on several legs compounds, so the joint's uncertainty band is much wider than any single leg's.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare pack probabilities computed at the morning injury report and at confirmed lineups and measure the change in Brier score of realised packs.

nonlinearities.shape: Hinge in |expected margin|: zero below about 6, strengthening above
nonlinearities.why: The minutes link between a cover leg and a star leg is zero until blowouts are plausible and then strengthens for starters of both teams (a function of |margin|), so the dependence cannot be a constant correlation; a side-signed expected margin feature would mis-specify it and only the usage effect should carry a side sign.

nonlinearities.shape: Tail dependence in the upper tail
nonlinearities.why: Hot-shooting nights lift all of a team's scorers at once, so joint overs have more mass in the extreme tail than a Gaussian copula with the same correlations.

nonlinearities.shape: Discrete non-Gaussian marginals
nonlinearities.why: Player counts at N+ thresholds are discrete with overdispersion; normal-score transformations must use the exact discrete CDF to avoid biasing joint probabilities.

contract.settlement_definition: Assist ladder markets settle Yes if the named player records at least N assists (strike 7.5 means 8+) in the single named game, using the player's final recorded assists. Two variants are live: KXNBAAST (unprotected) settles to a fair price if the player is inactive or active but never takes the court, and on actual assists once he enters; KXNBAASTPROT (protected) settles to the pre-tip fair price if the player enters in the first half but not after the first half (including overtime) unless he already has the required assists, and on actual statistics whenever he enters after the first half, regardless of first-half participation. A short postponement stays open; a game cancelled or not started within 48 hours resolves to fair price. Assists are an official-scorer statistic subject to later correction. The sampled KXNBAASTPROT secondary text is truncated at 600 characters in the evidence pack, so any inactive-player and overtime sentences that follow it were never seen.

rules_evidence.quote: If a player is inactive, or active but never takes the court, the market settles to a fair price.
rules_evidence.establishes: Unprotected DNP: a non-appearance is void at fair price rather than No, so the Yes probability is conditional on stepping onto the court.

rules_evidence.quote: Once a player enters the game the market settles based on the player's assists recorded.
rules_evidence.establishes: Once the player enters, for any length of time, the contract is a plain count; an early injury exit lowers the realised count and settles No when the strike is missed.

rules_evidence.quote: this Contract resolves to the fair price prior to the opening tip of the game unless the player records the required number of assists
rules_evidence.establishes: Protected variant voids a first-half-only appearance unless the strike is already reached, removing the injury-exit lower tail for that case.

rules_evidence.quote: records 8+ assists in the Minnesota vs New Orleans Pro Basketball game originally scheduled for Nov 6, 2026
rules_evidence.establishes: Strike is an integer 'N+' threshold (floor_strike 7.5) on one game's assist count, so adjacent rungs are survival probabilities of a discrete count.

variants_and_edge_cases: Protected versus unprotected: the same player and threshold can be listed under both tickers with different void sets, so the probabilities of Yes conditional on settlement differ.
Inactive versus active-but-no-minutes: both void at fair price in the unprotected rule, so late scratches affect edge accounting but not the settled count.

Overtime: the protected text mentions overtime only for the second-half-entry test ("including any overtime period"); whether overtime assists count toward the total is not stated in any sampled text and is assumed to follow official box-score totals (u5).
Assist credit is an official scorer judgement and is subject to post-game stat corrections that can flip a rung at the threshold.
Rungs run from 2+ to 12+ for different players; the same distribution should satisfy monotone survival across rungs.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official league box score assist totals (NBA.com), including later stat corrections.

mechanism.summary: An assist is credited when a player's pass directly leads to a made field goal by a teammate, so the count is (team made field goals while he is on court) x (share of those baskets he assisted). The first factor depends on how many minutes the player plays, how many possessions the team uses in that time, the team's shooting quality that night and its assisted share (isolation-heavy teams assist less); the second factor depends on his ball-handling role, how many other creators share the floor, and how often a pass becomes an assisted make as opposed to a missed shot, a turnover or an unassisted attack. Variation therefore comes from minutes (blowout and foul truncation), teammates' shooting luck (the largest single-game noise source), lineup composition (who finishes, who else creates) and scorer-credit judgement. The count is overdispersed with a right tail for primary creators, and the discrete threshold at 8+ amplifies small shifts in the mean, so P(N+) is far more sensitive to teammates' shooting variance than to the player's own skill noise.

stages.name: Court time of the creator
stages.description: Assists accrue only on court, so the number of possessions the lead ball handler plays is the opportunity base. Primary creators play 30-36 minutes in normal games but 24-28 when the game is decided, and leave early when injured; the unprotected contract voids only a zero-minute game and the protected one a first-half-only exit. Rest and load-management habits change the starting minutes. For the protected series the early-exit hazard (injury, ejection, or a coach resting the lead guard for the whole second half of a first-half blowout) sets the void probability and the conditional distribution of the settled count.
stages.distribution: Mixture of normal-game, truncated-blowout and early-exit regimes; sd of minutes about 5 for starters, and a point mass at zero minutes that is voided.

stages.name: Ball-handling volume and creation role
stages.description: Per minute, assist chances are produced by time of possession, touches, pick-and-roll initiations and passes; potential assists measure the pass leading to a shot attempt. Role matters: a lead guard might average roughly 10-14 potential assists per game and league-leading creators well into the high teens (recalled, unsourced, u1) while a wing averages 4-6. The presence of a co-creator (another high-usage ball handler) divides the initiations, and a missing co-creator increases the share.
stages.distribution: Potential assists per minute is stable (cross-game sd about 25% of the mean) and approximately Poisson-overdispersed per game.

stages.name: Team scoring environment and assisted-shot share
stages.description: The pool of assistable baskets is the team's made field goals, and the fraction that are assisted varies with style (ball-movement offences about 65-70%, isolation-heavy about 50-55%), shot type (threes and rim finishes are assisted at higher rates than pull-up twos) and the opponent's scheme (switching and pressure reduce clean passing lanes). The expected number of team assisted makes in the player's minutes is the volume he draws from.
stages.distribution: Team assisted FGM per game: mean about 26, sd about 4.5; positively correlated with team field-goal percentage that night.

stages.name: Conversion by teammates on the floor
stages.description: Potential assists become assists only if the teammate makes the shot, so the on-court teammates' shooting skill and shot quality set the conversion; hot or cold shooting from teammates is the largest noise term because a creator has no control over makes. With a major finisher absent, conversion drops even if potential assists stay the same, while with a creator absent the player's potential assists rise.
stages.distribution: Binomial conversion of 10-14 potential assists at p about 0.5-0.6, with additional between-game luck in teammate shooting (sd of about 6-8 percentage points); the product is overdispersed.

stages.name: Credit, distribution and rung probability
stages.description: The official scorer awards the assist by judgement (how many dribbles, whether the pass created the shot), with arena and scorer tendencies that move totals by about half an assist on average, and post-game corrections occasionally change a count. The resulting integer count is right-skewed and the rung probabilities P(N+) follow its survival function, with fair-price voids for non-appearance in the unprotected contract.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed discrete count (negative-binomial-like), variance ratio about 1.3-1.6 for guards, with scorer-level offsets of about 0.3-0.7 assists.

environment.note: Venue and altitude are not credible direct drivers of assist counts beyond the arena-level scorer credit effect captured in nba.scorer_bias; no separate environmental input for a passing statistic is justified.

game_context_script.note: Blowouts truncate minutes; close finishes add foul-driven possessions.

distribution_variance.note: Overdispersed count with luck from teammates.

settlement_contract.note: Fair-price voids and the protected clause.

nba.on_court_assist_share.label: On-court assist share of team assisted field goals
nba.on_court_assist_share.mechanism: The fraction of the team's assisted makes credited to the player while he is on the floor, which is the stable per-opportunity rate.
nba.on_court_assist_share.rationale: Potential assists and usage are indirect; the on-court assist share is the direct outcome rate, decomposed by lineup and whether co-creators are present, and is the cleanest basis for projecting the count from team assisted makes.
nba.on_court_assist_share.measurement: Share = player AST / (team assisted FGM while player on court), computed over last 60 games with half-life 25 games, separately for lineups with and without the top co-creator; shrink to role prior with k=300 on-court team assisted FGM; projected AST = share × expected team assisted FGM in projected minutes; as-of last game.
raw_data: Play-by-play with assist credit and lineups
nba.on_court_assist_share.why: The product of share and expected team assisted makes gives the mean directly and exposes how teammates' shooting enters.

nba.team_assisted_fgm_expectation.label: Expected team assisted field goals in the player's minutes
nba.team_assisted_fgm_expectation.mechanism: Team assisted makes depend on possessions, field-goal percentage, shot mix and the style-driven assisted rate.
nba.team_assisted_fgm_expectation.rationale: The draft uses implied team totals (market-derived) as the environment; an own estimate of assisted makes depends on assisted-rate by team and by opponent coverage, which totals do not capture.
nba.team_assisted_fgm_expectation.measurement: E[assisted FGM] = possessions(own pace composition) × FGA per possession × FG% (opponent-adjusted, 20-game half-life, k=150 FGA) × assisted rate (team assisted/FGM, opponent scheme adjustment, 20-game half-life, k=100 FGM); scale to player's projected minutes share; report mean and sd by game.
nba.team_assisted_fgm_expectation.why: Replaces a market-derived environment with an own estimate focused on assisted makes, the quantity assists actually count.

nba.co_creator_load.label: Co-creator load (ball-dominant teammates on court)
nba.co_creator_load.mechanism: The presence of another ball-dominant creator divides initiations and assists.
nba.co_creator_load.rationale: Usage alone cannot distinguish a lone primary creator from a two-creator backcourt; assists fall when the second creator is on the floor and rise when he is out.
nba.co_creator_load.measurement: For the player and each teammate compute time of possession and touches per minute over 60 games; co-creator load = sum of the other four players' expected time of possession per minute (from lineup minutes) minus the league-average of the role; regress player's potential assists per minute on load (ridge) with team fixed effects; compute with tonight's expected lineups and scenarios.
free_sources: NBA.com tracking time of possession (via nba_api)
raw_data: Player time of possession and touches per minute (tracking, cumulative with DateTo)
nba.co_creator_load.why: Directly addresses 'who else creates', the main role redistribution for assists that teammate absence alone cannot split.

nba.early_exit_hazard.label: Protected-void probability: first-half-only participation (injury, ejection, illness or coach-rested second half)
nba.early_exit_hazard.mechanism: P(player enters in the first half but never after halftime, including OT) = injury/ejection/illness exit hazard plus the coach decision to rest him for the whole second half in a lopsided game; the protected clause voids both unless the strike was already reached.
nba.early_exit_hazard.rationale: Early exit by injury is only one route to the void state: the sampled protected text voids any player who enters in the first half and does not enter after it, so a starter pulled for the entire second half of a first-half blowout is also void. Both routes are unrelated to per-minute rates and the second is strongly tied to the first-half margin.
nba.early_exit_hazard.measurement: Two components over the last 3 seasons. (a) Injury/ejection/illness exit hazard h = exits (left and did not return) / minutes, shrunk to a position prior with k=2000 minutes and scaled by 1.5 for the first 3 games after a listed injury; P(exit before half) = 1 - exp(-h*minutes_in_half1). (b) Coach-rest route: from play-by-play, P(no second-half entry | played first half and non-injury) by own-model pregame spread bucket and coach, estimated on 3 seasons with beta shrinkage k=30 games; combine as 1-(1-a)(1-b); then convert by contract wording (protected void vs actual stats, with the strike-already-reached carve-out).
nba.early_exit_hazard.why: The protected KXNBAASTPROT contract voids a first-half-only appearance (injury or a coach resting the creator through a blowout second half); this input gives P(void) and conditions the settled distribution, and the unprotected KXNBAAST needs only the zero-minute part.

nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.label: Ratings-based blowout probability and starter-minutes-vs-margin curve (market-free)
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.mechanism: Rebuilds the blowout risk from team strength and rotation history instead of the closing spread: a ratings-implied expected margin and margin spread give P(large lead), and a coach/player minutes-versus-margin curve converts each margin path into expected minutes lost by starters and gained by bench players.
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.rationale: The catalog input nba.garbage is defined from the closing spread, which is a market price and so a benchmark, not an input. The causal quantity is the chance that the margin passes the coach's pull threshold early enough to matter, and how much playing time each player then loses. Subtle: the loss depends on when the lead arrives (a 20-point lead entering Q4 removes far more starter minutes than one reached with 3 minutes left), on the coach, and on whether the trailing team also pulls starters, so the curve must be conditional on the margin path and not only on the final margin.
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.measurement: Step 1, expected margin: mu = (NetRtg_home_adj - NetRtg_away_adj) * expected_possessions/100 + home_adv, where NetRtg_adj is the as-of-tipoff opponent-adjusted net rating from nba.off_rtg and nba.def_rtg (ridge regression on game point differential, half-life about 25 games, shrunk to the preseason prior with n_prior about 20 games as a placeholder to be fitted), adjusted for the confirmed unavailable players via nba.lineup_adj_rating, home_adv fitted on the last 5 seasons (about 2 points). Step 2, margin spread: sd_margin fitted on 5 seasons of residuals of final margin versus mu (league-wide roughly 12-13 points, to be estimated, with a heavier empirical tail than normal). Step 3: P(final |margin| >= 15/20/25) and P(|lead| >= 15/20 entering Q4) from the empirical residual distribution around mu. Step 4, minutes curve: from play-by-play stints, per team-season, expected minutes of each rotation player conditional on margin entering Q4 in bins (0-9, 10-14, 15-19, 20+), shrunk toward the league curve with k about 30 blowout games. Output per player: expected minutes lost and the probability of falling below a stated minutes level. No closing line or other price is used; the spread is retained only to benchmark calibration of step 3.

nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.why: Replaces the spread-based nba.garbage in player_assists: blowout truncation of the relevant players' minutes from own ratings and the coach's pull curve, with no closing line used.
raw_data: team-game final margins and opponent-adjusted ratings as of tipoff (5 seasons)

nba.minutes.reason: Assists accrue per minute on court, and the minutes distribution including blowout truncation is the first factor; point projection hides the tail.

nba.pot_ast.reason: Potential assists per minute is the stable opportunity measure; it duplicates the tracking entry in content, and its tracking provenance limits free access.

nba.touches.reason: Touches and time of possession drive passes but are noisy proxies for creation; informative mainly for secondary creators.

nba.usage.reason: Usage (shot attempts and turnovers) is an offensive-load measure; for assists it is partly inversely related for creators who score, so assist share is the right measure instead.

nba.teammate_conv.reason: Conversion of potential assists into makes is the largest noise source, and regressing it to talent is correct; needs lineup-conditional estimates.

nba.teammate_absence_shift.reason: Finisher versus creator absence has opposite effects; the single with/without delta is only useful if split into creation share and conversion.

nba.opp_ast_allowed.reason: Opponent assisted-FG allowed by role is a direct pass-lane measure; small sample per role limits precision.

nba.def_scheme.reason: Switching and blitz change passing lanes but evidence is weak; effect already partly inside opponent assists allowed.

nba.pace.reason: Possessions scale chances, but only in proportion to time on ball in transition; effect is role-dependent.

nba.implied_team_totals.reason: Derived from sportsbook spread and total; replace with an own-model assisted-FGM environment and keep this as a benchmark.

nba.garbage.reason: Catalog definition is 'Blowout / garbage-time probability from spread' (measurement: P(final |margin| > 15/20/25) as a function of the closing spread), so as defined it is market-derived and only a calibration benchmark; the blowout-minutes mechanism is carried by the market-free nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve (ratings-implied margin plus coach minutes-versus-margin curve).

nba.rest_travel.reason: Back-to-back effects work mainly through minutes and rest decisions; small direct effect on assist rate.

nba.scorer_bias.reason: Arena scorer credit varies by about half an assist, a real but small offset useful only after other factors.

nba.injuries_pit.reason: Own and teammates' status determines minutes, creators and finishers on court; vintage relative to the quote is crucial.

nba.stat_dist.reason: The overdispersed count distribution converts mean into rung probabilities; must be fitted per role, not pooled.

nba.stat_corrections.reason: Post-game corrections matter only for labels near the strike; no pregame effect.

nba.tracking.reason: Described as a data source (speed, defender distance); its assist-relevant content is potential assists and time of possession already counted in pot_ast and touches.

nba.player_role_position.reason: Role classification determines the prior for pass share and who steps up when teammates are out, but is categorical and coarse.

nba.late_game_script.reason: Close games add intentional-foul possessions that mostly affect free throws; effect on assists is weak.

m.quote_history.reason: Kalshi price path for the assist ladder; useful to see when information was absorbed and for calibration labels, but it is an observation of the market, never an explanatory driver of the outcome.

interactions.mechanism: A missing finisher cuts conversion while potential assists stay constant, a missing creator raises the player's potential assists, so the direction of the absence effect on assists depends on the absent player's role; a single dummy averages opposite effects to zero.
interactions.how_to_test: Split absence games by absent-player role and regress assists on potential assists and teammate shooting separately.

interactions.mechanism: A lead guard on a heavy favourite loses late minutes, which removes the upper rungs; effect appears beyond a expected margin threshold near 8-10 and concentrates in the 9+ assist rungs.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare P(9+ assists) in expected margin buckets for guards controlling for per-minute rate.

interactions.mechanism: Potential assists per minute scale with the share of initiations the player owns, so doubling co-creator load roughly halves his share; the effect is multiplicative on the per-minute rate and larger for players who rely on on-ball time.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress log potential assists per minute on log co-creator load with player fixed effects.

interactions.mechanism: Switch-heavy defences reduce assisted baskets for pick-and-roll creators more than for off-ball movers, so the opponent effect depends on the creator's primary action; ranking by raw assists allowed hides that.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact opponent coverage with the player's pick-and-roll initiation share.

interactions.mechanism: Teammate shooting luck is common to all of a creator's potential assists in the game, so assists have a variance larger than a binomial with independent makes; this variance is shared with teammates' scoring props.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare residual variance of assists with a binomial benchmark and correlate residuals with team three-point percentage.

nonlinearities.shape: Hinge near a 9-point expected margin, concave after
nonlinearities.why: Minutes for lead ball handlers fall steeply once starters are expected to sit; extra expected margin beyond about 14 changes little since the starters are already out.

nonlinearities.shape: Regression toward talent with a shrinkage weight near 0.6-0.7 for a 10-game sample
nonlinearities.why: Hot team shooting of the last 10 games overstates conversion; the response of future assists to recent conversion is much flatter than one.

nonlinearities.shape: Right-skewed overdispersed with heavier tail for primary creators
nonlinearities.why: A guard with a mean of 7.5 has more mass at 12+ than a Poisson, so high rungs are less steeply priced than a simple model implies.

nonlinearities.shape: Diminishing conversion at high potential-assist counts
nonlinearities.why: When the number of potential assists is very high the marginal pass is lower quality, so assists rise less than proportionally in games with extreme potential assists.

contract.settlement_definition: Four live series; three have recovered rules text and KXNBAPLAYTOGETHER is TITLE_ONLY. KXNBASTARTERS: Yes only if the named player starts his team's first 2026-27 regular-season game and is on the floor at the opening tip; an announced starter who does not actually start resolves No; resolution is based solely on who starts that game, regardless of a retirement, signing or trade beforehand. KXNBARETURN: Yes if the named player enters a game for the named team inside a stated window (sampled: after May 28 and before Jun 20, 2026, i.e. late playoff rounds), so the team must still be playing. KXNBACOMPETE: Yes if the named player enters any 2026-27 regular-season NBA game for at least one second; preseason and playoff games do not count (sampled for an unsigned veteran, so a signing is required first). KXNBAPLAYTOGETHER: definition (same game versus shared minutes) is not visible (CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS).

rules_evidence.quote: must start the first regular season game for Minnesota and be on the floor at the time of the opening tip-off
rules_evidence.establishes: The starter market is one specific game with a strict physical test (on the floor at opening tip), so an announced starter who is scratched at the last minute resolves No, not void.

rules_evidence.quote: If Terrence Shannon Jr. is announced as a starter for the first regular season game for Minnesota but doesn't actually start the game due to injury or any other reason, the market resolves to No.
rules_evidence.establishes: An announced starter who is scratched or benched at the tip resolves No, not void, so the residual risk between confirmation and tip is fully borne by the Yes side.

rules_evidence.quote: must enter the game for at least one second in any regular season game in the 2026-27 season. Preseason and playoff games do not count towards this market.
rules_evidence.establishes: Compete means any regular-season appearance of at least one second; for an unsigned player the event requires signing, health and a coach's decision to play him, with playoffs and preseason excluded.

rules_evidence.quote: must enter a game for the Knicks after May 28, 2026 and before Jun 20, 2026.
rules_evidence.establishes: Return means entering a game for the named team inside a fixed window, so the team's remaining games in that window (playoff survival) multiply the recovery probability.

variants_and_edge_cases: Clock mismatch within the key: first-game starter (one decision at opening night), return (enter a game for the named team inside a dated window), compete (any regular-season appearance across a season, for an unsigned player) and play together (title only) are different processes sharing one label.
Announced versus actual: the starter market resolves No if an announced starter does not take the floor at the tip, so confirmation 30 minutes before tip still leaves a small residual risk.

Return windows in late May and June fall in the conference finals and Finals: if the team is eliminated before the player is healthy, there are no games left and the market resolves No regardless of health.
Compete excludes preseason and playoff games and counts a single second of play; a signing late in the season with few games left sharply reduces exposure.
KXNBAPLAYTOGETHER has no rules text: whether 'together' means the same game or overlapping minutes, and the window, are unseen (u1).
contract.settlement_data_source: Official starting lineup and play-by-play (starter, entries), official box scores for appearances; rules name no explicit source.

mechanism.summary: These markets ask whether a player will be present in a particular role or state, and the four live series are three different processes plus one unseen one. First-game starter (KXNBASTARTERS): a coach's discrete choice among a roster after training camp, constrained by health, a minutes plan and the team's lineup philosophy, settled by who is on the floor at the opening tip; information arrives in preseason lineups, camp reports and a pre-tip confirmation. Return (KXNBARETURN): an injury-recovery time-to-event that only pays if the team still has games inside the dated window, so recovery is multiplied by playoff survival game by game. Compete (KXNBACOMPETE, sampled for an unsigned veteran): a signing must happen first, then the coach must give him at least one second in a regular-season game, so it is a signing hazard times the regular-season games left after the signing. Play-together (KXNBAPLAYTOGETHER, title only): the overlap of two players' availability, positively correlated through shared team rest decisions. Across all of them the common ingredients are the injury status timeline, role decisions and exposure windows, and the sharp tails come from discrete decisions (a signing, a coach's lineup card, an elimination) rather than smooth rates. The rare-make accrual mechanism left this key with KXNBAONE3PT (now in season_stat_markets), and next-team transactions left with KXNBANEXTTEAM/KXNBANEXTTEAMCONF (now in off_court_events).

stages.name: Health state and recovery timeline
stages.description: Every variant begins with whether the player is healthy: a return market is a time-to-event on recovery with a published timeline and uncertainty, a starter market requires him to be healthy for the opener, and a compete market requires him to be fit enough to sign and appear in at least one regular-season game. Reported timelines are lower bounds more often than expected, setbacks occur in a fraction of cases, and restrictions after return reduce minutes. The hazard of recovery depends on the injury type and on the team's disclosure style.
stages.distribution: Time-to-event with Weibull-like shape: slow start, peak near the stated timeline, long right tail from setbacks; about 20-30% of returns slip beyond the first stated date (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED).

stages.name: Coach role decision and rotation
stages.description: For the starter market the coach chooses five from the roster given health, camp performance, lineup chemistry and the game-one opponent; incumbents start unless displaced by an addition, an injury or a strategic change (small-ball, defence-first). For the compete market a signed veteran still needs the coach to use him for one second in a regular-season game, which is likely but not certain for an end-of-bench signing, and for play-together markets the rotation determines whether two players share minutes. KXNBASTARTERS is itself a single-game contract (verified rules and API: start the team's first 2026-27 regular-season game and be on the floor at the opening tip; announced-but-not-starting resolves No), so the game-level starter mechanism is live inside this archetype once per season, consistent with the catalog label 'starting lineup / player availability'.
stages.distribution: Discrete choice over the roster with strong incumbency (starters last season retain the role about 80% of the time, SOURCE_UNVERIFIED); role changes cluster in the off-season.

stages.name: Signing of an unsigned player (compete market)
stages.description: KXNBACOMPETE (sampled for Ben Simmons, an unsigned veteran) requires a regular-season appearance, so the player must first sign with an NBA team. That depends on his health and perceived value, on which teams have a roster spot and minimum-salary room, on the timing (pre-camp signings, mid-season injury-replacement signings, post-deadline buyout market) and on alternatives abroad. After signing, the coach must play him at least one second in a regular-season game. Next-team markets that once used this stage moved to off_court_events.
stages.distribution: Low-rate signing hazard over the season with bumps at training camp, injury waves and the buyout window; conditional on signing, appearance probability is high but not 1.

stages.name: Exposure window: team games available inside the window
stages.description: Return and compete markets need games to happen while the player is available. For KXNBARETURN the sampled window (May 28 to Jun 20) covers the conference finals and Finals, so the number of team games left is a random variable from series survival and length, and P(Yes) = sum over remaining games of P(team still playing that game) x P(recovered and used by then). For KXNBACOMPETE the exposure is the regular-season games left after a signing date. A player cleared one day after elimination resolves No.
stages.distribution: Product of a recovery time-to-event and a decreasing survival curve of team games; mass at zero when the team is eliminated early or the signing never happens.

stages.name: Joint presence and wording filters
stages.description: Play-together and starter markets depend on two or more players being simultaneously present or in specified roles, which makes the events correlated through team rest and injury policy. Wording filters (first regular-season game, on the floor at the tip, regular-season games only) set which observable counts. A single injured teammate or a coach's rest decision applies to both players, so joint presence is more variable than independent presence.
stages.distribution: Joint Bernoulli with positive dependence between rest decisions; regime effects when the stated window is short.

talent_strength.note: The core question is presence and role, not performance level; talent enters only through the coach's choice (who is better) which is covered by nba.starter_probability, and has no separate strength input for these markets.

opponent_matchup.note: Opponent identity matters little for season-level or opening-night presence markets; the first-game starter market could depend on opponent size but no evidence supports a measurable effect.

environment.note: Venue, altitude and travel do not drive these presence markets beyond the minor schedule fatigue effect handled in rest and load management inputs.

game_context_script.note: In-game script changes minutes but not whether a player starts, returns or appears for one second; the relevant game-level context is whether the team still has games in the window, which is carried in stage s4 by nba.series_model.

pace_volume.note: The only volume that matters is exposure: the number of team games inside the KXNBARETURN window (series survival and length) and the regular-season games left after a KXNBACOMPETE signing; no possession or attempt count enters any live contract.

efficiency_conversion.note: No live series settles on converting shots or opportunities: starter, return, compete and play-together outcomes are presence events, and the rare-three accrual that needed a make rate left with KXNBAONE3PT.

distribution_variance.note: Weibull-type recovery times with a setback tail, and positively correlated joint presence for the play-together pair.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Season-level rest and incentive effects work through nba.load_mgmt (rest and return-from-injury policy) and late-season nba.standings_motivation; daily back-to-back context (nba.rest_travel) is audited IRRELEVANT for these season-level and one-time markets and is no longer a stage or coverage input.

officiating_rules.note: Referee behaviour has no bearing on a player's role, return or destination; the only rule-like element is the exposure window (season type filter) handled under settlement.

settlement_contract.note: Rules text for starter (on floor at tip, announced-but-not-starting is No), return (enter a game for the team inside a dated window) and compete (any regular-season second; preseason/playoffs excluded); play-together is title only (u1).

nba.return_timeline_hazard.label: Return-from-injury timeline hazard by injury type
nba.return_timeline_hazard.mechanism: The probability a player has returned by a date follows a recovery time-to-event distribution with setbacks, not a point estimate.
nba.return_timeline_hazard.rationale: Reported timelines are lower bounds with setbacks; a return-by-date market is a CDF at a date, and the shape depends on the injury (ankle sprain versus stress fracture versus surgery).
nba.return_timeline_hazard.measurement: For each injury event 2015-present define t = days from the first public report date to first game appearance (right-censored at season end). Fit a Weibull survival model per injury category (ankle, knee, hamstring, back, foot/fracture, surgery, illness) with parameters shrunk to the pooled category with k=8 events, plus covariates: stated timeline (log days), team disclosure ratio (team's median actual/stated duration over its prior 10 events, shrunk to 1 with k=5) and age. P(return by T) = 1 - exp(-(t_T/scale)^shape) where t_T = days from the report date to T conditional on survival to the as-of day (use the conditional survival). Update at each new report; as-of timestamp = latest report vintage before the decision.
raw_data: injury events with injury date, report date, stated timeline, first-return date
nba.return_timeline_hazard.why: The return market is a CDF of recovery time and cannot be read from a status label.

nba.opening_night_starter_signals.label: Opening-night starter signals (camp lineups, preseason starts, coach statements)
nba.opening_night_starter_signals.mechanism: The first regular-season game's starting five is predicted from the preseason starting lineups, camp reports and coach statements, with strong incumbency.
nba.opening_night_starter_signals.rationale: A season-opener market has no in-season history, so the signal is the preseason; the team's preseason starters in the final two preseason games are usually the opener's starters, but not always.
nba.opening_night_starter_signals.measurement: Score for each player = 0.5 x indicator of starting both of the last 2 preseason games + 0.3 x last season's start share + 0.2 x coach statement (coded 0/0.5/1); map to probability via logistic fit on 8 seasons of opener starters; set to 0 if the status is out or doubtful; combine with injury probability; as-of 24 hours before the opener and again at confirmation.
free_sources: Preseason box scores (nba_api season type Pre Season)
nba.opening_night_starter_signals.why: The market is a single decision with an info set that is preseason only; the draft's starter probability input does not specify its sources.

nba.player_move_destination_model.label: Player destination choice model with cap feasibility
nba.player_move_destination_model.mechanism: Destination is a choice among feasible teams determined by cap space or matching assets, team need, and player preference.
nba.player_move_destination_model.rationale: A multi-outcome next-team market needs a distribution over teams; relying on rumor misses cap constraints that exclude most teams.
nba.player_move_destination_model.measurement: For each candidate team compute feasibility (cap space or matching salaries within apron rules), asset fit and need (position gap, win-now vs rebuild); estimate a multinomial logit on 10 seasons of moves with these features plus player-preference flags (stated preference, agent reports); add a catch-all with probability from age and contract status; as-of nightly.
raw_data: Team payroll and cap state by date
nba.player_move_destination_model.why: Next-team markets are multinomial and the feasibility screen removes impossible teams before probabilities are assigned.

nba.co_appearance_overlap_prob.label: Two-player co-appearance probability with rest correlation
nba.co_appearance_overlap_prob.mechanism: The probability that both players appear in at least one same game (or in many) is a joint availability probability with positive dependence from team rest decisions.
nba.co_appearance_overlap_prob.rationale: Treating two players' availability as independent overstates co-appearance when rest decisions are shared and understates it when injuries are independent.
nba.co_appearance_overlap_prob.measurement: Per game, P(both play) = pA pB + rho sqrt(pA(1-pA)pB(1-pB)) with rho estimated from 5 seasons of pair data (team rest days, load management) shrunk to a role prior; over N games P(at least one overlap) = 1 - Π(1 - P_g) with a correction for injury duration (autocorrelation across games); update after each game.
nba.co_appearance_overlap_prob.why: Play-together markets are about the joint presence of two players, not each one alone.

nba.unsigned_player_signing_hazard.label: Unsigned-player NBA signing and activation hazard
nba.unsigned_player_signing_hazard.mechanism: An unsigned veteran appears in a regular-season game only after a team signs him and plays him; signings cluster at camp, injury waves and the buyout window.
nba.unsigned_player_signing_hazard.rationale: KXNBACOMPETE needs at least one second of regular-season play by an unsigned player, so the probability is P(sign before the season's last games) x P(play | signed); health and perceived value drive the signing, and a late signing leaves few games, which a generic availability input does not model.
nba.unsigned_player_signing_hazard.measurement: Reference class: players unsigned on a given calendar date (Oct 15, Dec 1, Feb 1) with age >=26 and >=500 NBA minutes in the previous season, 2010-2026. Monthly signing hazard by discrete-time logistic regression on age, last-season minutes and games, injury flag and star-draft status, shrunk to the pooled hazard with k=10 players; drop the 'interest reports' feature unless captured with a timestamp. P(play | signed) = share of such signings with regular-season minutes, and days to first appearance by survival; combine across remaining months to P(signs by date) and P(plays by date). As-of: market snapshot, using the free-agent list as of that date only.
raw_data: player age, last-season minutes and games, injury status
nba.unsigned_player_signing_hazard.why: Gives the signing-then-appearance probability for KXNBACOMPETE.

nba.starters_pit.reason: The live KXNBASTARTERS series is a finalized opening-night market that settles on the state at the tip, so the 30-minute-before-tip confirmation vintage only trims residual last-second risk; it is primary for in-season starter markets, which have no live series in the evidence pack, and secondary for the live contract.

nba.injuries_pit.reason: Report vintage and status drive every variant (return, starter, exposure); needs the recovery timeline shape instead of a status label.

nba.status_resolution_prob.reason: Game-level questionable-to-play calibration is useful for the opener and for returns, but it is defined for a single game and not for a season accumulation.

nba.starter_probability.reason: The right object for the starter market but without a specified source for the opener; preseason signals are required.

nba.load_mgmt.reason: Rest policy lowers exposure for the one-three accrual and for co-appearance markets, but is hard to forecast for a full season.

nba.rotation.reason: Coach rotation habits affect the starter and role decisions; defined by margin-conditional minutes, which is mostly a within-game concept.

nba.rest_travel.reason: Back-to-back context is a single-game availability driver; the live series are season-level or one-time decisions where daily rest is secondary to injury or role.

nba.standings_motivation.reason: Team stakes affect whether a contender signs an unsigned veteran mid-season (compete market) only loosely; the next-team markets that used it moved to off_court_events.

nba.news.reason: Reporter signals and transactions are relevant to next-team markets but, without source reliability and stage, the entry cannot produce a probability.

m.quote_history.reason: Kalshi price path for the player-status contracts; useful to see when information was absorbed and for calibration labels, but it is an observation of the market, never an explanatory driver of the outcome.

m.rules_text.reason: Versioned rules text defines the settled quantity for the player-status contracts; wording changes between series are the only way to know the target variable, so it is a required contract input, not a feature.

m.lifecycle.reason: Market open/close/expiration timing for the player-status contracts defines the information horizon at which any estimate must be as-of; context only.
