contract.settlement_definition: Eleven live series, all with recovered rules text. Player head-to-heads (KXNBAH2HPRA, KXNBAH2HPTS, KXNBAH2H3PT): Yes if player A records more of the stat than player B 'in the full game'; an exact tie with both players entering resolves 50/50; if either player does not enter, or the game is cancelled or postponed more than two weeks, fair price. Series totals (KXNBASERIESPTS): at least N points over the entire named series; regulation and overtime count; stats final at series end (later corrections ignored); a player who enters no game resolves to fair price. Every-game runs (KXNBAPTSALLGAMES 25+, KXNBA3PTALLGAMES 2+): the threshold must be met in every game of the series; a game not entered resolves the market No; overtime counts. Series leaders (KXNBASERIESPTSLEADER, REBLEADER, ASTLEADER, 3PMLEADER): Yes if the player records the most of the stat over the series; a player entering no game resolves to fair price; ties pay $1/N (rounded down to the cent) to Yes. Summer League (KXNBASUMMERPTS): N+ points in a named Summer League game; active but never entering settles at the last fair price before game start.

rules_evidence.quote: If both players enter the game and record an equal number of combined points, rebounds, and assists, then all markets resolve to 50/50.
rules_evidence.establishes: A tie settles at 50/50, so the tie mass is worth half a contract to each side rather than No or a void.

rules_evidence.quote: If one or both players do not enter the Cleveland vs New York professional basketball game originally scheduled for May 22, 2026, or the game is cancelled or postponed more than two weeks
rules_evidence.establishes: If either player does not enter, or the game slips more than two weeks, the market resolves to a fair price, so both players' availability is a void state, not a loss, and the postponement window is two weeks, not 48 hours.

rules_evidence.quote: If both players enter the game and record an equal number of made three pointers, then all markets resolve to 50/50.
rules_evidence.establishes: The threes head-to-head uses the same 50/50 tie rule as PRA, so the 12-20% exact-tie mass for made threes is split, not lost.

rules_evidence.quote: If one or both players do not enter the New York vs San Antonio professional basketball game originally scheduled for Jun 13, 2026, or the game is cancelled or postponed more than two weeks, then all markets resolve to a fair market price.
rules_evidence.establishes: Non-entry by either player voids at fair price for the points head-to-head too, so availability is a void state for all three H2H series.

rules_evidence.quote: Statistics recorded during both regulation time and overtime count. If a player does not enter any game during the series, then all markets for that player resolve to a fair market price.
rules_evidence.establishes: Series totals include overtime and void only if the player never plays; missing some games lowers the total but does not void.

rules_evidence.quote: Note: If a player does not enter a game during the series, then the market for that player resolve to No.
rules_evidence.establishes: For every-game runs a missed game is a loss, not a void, so per-game availability enters the run probability directly.

rules_evidence.quote: If multiple players are tied for the most made three pointers at the end of the series, “Yes” positions will pay $1/N (rounded down to the nearest cent), where N is the number of tied participants
rules_evidence.establishes: Leader ties pay 1/N; for low-count stats such as made threes ties at the top are frequent, so the payout is fractional in a material share of outcomes.

rules_evidence.quote: If a player is active but never takes the court, the market settles to the last fair market price before game start.
rules_evidence.establishes: Summer League points ladders void at the pre-game fair price for an active non-participant; once he enters, actual points settle.

variants_and_edge_cases: Head-to-head ties resolve 50/50 when both enter (PRA, points, threes); Skellam-type tie mass for made threes is about 12-20% at means of 2-5 each (Poisson arithmetic gives 13-21%, overdispersion lowers it), smaller for points and PRA.

Non-entry handling differs by series type: H2H fair price if either player does not enter; series total and leader fair price only if the player enters no game; every-game runs resolve No on any missed game.
Series-level stats are final at series end and later corrections are ignored; overtime counts in series totals and every-game runs; H2H says 'full game' (overtime implied, not stated).
Series length is random (4 to 7 games) and every game of the series counts, so totals rise and every-game runs fall with length.
Leader ties pay $1/N rounded down to the cent; the leader field is all players of both teams.
Summer League ladders are single-game 'N+' points with a pre-game fair-price void for active non-participants; minute plans and participation choices dominate.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official box scores per game (NBA.com / NBA Summer League); series stats final at series conclusion per the rules.

mechanism.summary: The three variants share one structure: a comparison or accumulation of player-game counts where the quantity of interest is the distribution of a difference or a sum rather than a threshold on one count. For a head-to-head the difference X_A - X_B has a mean given by the two players' expected counts and a variance that depends on each count's variance and on their correlation, which differs by pair type: same-team players are negatively associated at fixed team output because they split the same shots, rebounds and assists, opposing players are positively associated through shared pace, and players in different games are independent. A tie is possible for integer counts and its probability depends on the discreteness. For a series, the sum runs over a random number of games (the series length is itself uncertain and depends on the team strengths), each game's minutes are inflated in the playoffs, injuries attrite exposure, and the games are not independent because opposing coaches adjust. Summer League adds unstable rosters, announced minute plans, and rookies who play a fraction of the games. So the key information is exposure (games and minutes), dependence between the two sides, and discreteness at ties. Two further live series types are not pairwise: a series stat leader is the maximum of many players' cumulative totals over a random number of shared games, and points in every game is a run of threshold hits that any cold night or missed game breaks (stage s6).

stages.name: Exposure: games played and presence of both players
stages.description: Both players must play for a comparison to be meaningful, and in a series the number of games played by each depends on series length, injuries and rest decisions. A star out for part of a series reduces his total; the head-to-head may void or favour the player who plays. Exposure is the product of the number of games in the series (random) and the probability of availability in each game (autocorrelated through injuries).
stages.distribution: Series length P(4,5,6,7) with mean about 5.7 for evenly matched teams and 4.8 for mismatches; availability per game with persistence across games.

stages.name: Minutes and role in each game
stages.description: For each player the minutes mixture defines how many opportunities he has; in the playoffs the rotation tightens and stars play 38-42 minutes, so per-game counts inflate relative to the regular season, while in Summer League minutes are set by a plan, rookies may be capped and veterans may be rested in back-to-back games. Minutes are correlated across the two players when they are teammates in the same blowout or in opposing teams in the same game flow.
stages.distribution: Truncated normal in the playoffs (sd 3-4 minutes) versus bimodal in Summer League (limited or full minutes); correlation of minutes between the two players depends on the pair type.

stages.name: Per-minute rates and the opponent assignment
stages.description: Per-minute stat rates come from the player's usage and role, adjusted for the opponent's defence by position and, in series, by the primary defender assigned to him; the playoff matchup assignments suppress or boost a star's counts in a way not visible in regular-season splits. Across games in a series coaches adjust coverage so the effect changes over the series.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed counts around a rate that is itself shifted by matchup assignments; matchup shifts of 5-15% of the stat in a series (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED).

stages.name: Dependence between the two counts and ties
stages.description: The difference distribution depends on the correlation of the two players' counts: for opposing players it is positive through pace and through shared game script, shrinking the difference variance; for teammates it is negative at fixed team output (one player's shot is not the other's) but positive through team pace, so the net sign depends on the stat. With integer counts, ties have positive probability, 12-20% for made threes and a bit lower for assists, and the tie rule matters.
stages.distribution: Difference of two overdispersed counts with correlation from about -0.2 (teammates, shot-based stats) to +0.3 (opponents, pace-driven stats); discrete with a mass at zero.

stages.name: Summer League and series settlement structure
stages.description: Summer League points ladders (KXNBASUMMERPTS, 'N+' in one game) hinge on roster churn, unannounced minute plans and game participation (top picks play two or three games, others play five), with a pre-game fair-price void if the player is active but does not enter; scoring rate is the rookie's or prospect's usage at Summer League level. For series totals (KXNBASERIESPTS) the settled quantity is the sum over all games the player enters in a random-length series, with overtime included and a void only if he enters none, so the pmf is a compound distribution over games played.
stages.distribution: Compound distribution (random games times random per-game counts); Summer League participation is a discrete choice with strong draft-slot dependence.

stages.name: Series leader maximum and every-game threshold runs
stages.description: Series leaders for points, rebounds, assists and made threes are the argmax of cumulative totals across both rosters over four to seven games, decided among the top producers by expected per-game rate times games played; ties pay 1/N, which matters most for made threes where top totals are small integers. Every-game runs (25+ points, 2+ threes) need the threshold in each game of a random-length series and any missed game is a No, so a longer series lowers them geometrically, a cold-shooting or foul-trouble night breaks them, and per-game hits are positively correlated through role and health; the threes run is much more fragile because per-game threes are low-count and overdispersed.
stages.distribution: Leader: categorical over about six serious candidates, sharper than a single-game leader because summing 4-7 games cuts noise. Every-game: product of correlated per-game Bernoullis over a 4-7 game random length, so mass falls roughly geometrically in series length.

talent_strength.note: Player rates in the named stat.

opponent_matchup.note: Opponent defence by position and playoff assignments.

availability_news.note: Both players' status and exposure over a series.

environment.note: Venue and altitude affect both players in the same game in the same way for opposing pairs and are second-order for a comparison of two counts; no separate environmental input is justified.

efficiency_conversion.note: Shooting-luck regression of recent 3P% or FG% toward talent and shot quality sets the per-attempt rate for threes and points comparisons; its extension to series-long shrinkage is untested (u4).

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest, game selection and series elimination states.

officiating_rules.note: Referee crew effects on foul-based stats exist but are shared by both players in a game for opposing pairs, and no separate officiating input is justified for a difference between two counts.

settlement_contract.note: All 11 series have rules text: H2H 50/50 ties and fair-price non-entry; series totals include OT and void only with zero games; every-game runs lose on a missed game; leaders pay 1/N on ties; Summer League void at pre-game fair price.

nba.pair_difference_correlation.label: Pair-type correlation of player stat residuals
nba.pair_difference_correlation.mechanism: The correlation between two players' counts differs by pair type (teammates, opponents, separate games) and by stat.
nba.pair_difference_correlation.rationale: The draft says positive correlation through game script, but for teammates the allocation effect is negative; a single sign misprices the difference variance and tie mass.
nba.pair_difference_correlation.measurement: For stat s and pair type, compute the correlation of residuals (after removing player and opponent effects and minutes) over 5 seasons for pairs of similar roles; pool in role-pair cells with shrinkage k=60 games; report the correlation and the implied variance of the difference var = var_A + var_B - 2 rho sd_A sd_B; produce P(A > B), P(tie), P(B > A) via a bivariate negative-binomial.
raw_data: Player-game stats with team and opponent
nba.pair_difference_correlation.why: Head-to-head price depends mostly on the difference variance and tie mass, which the correlation sets.

nba.series_player_exposure.label: Expected games and minutes exposure over a series
nba.series_player_exposure.mechanism: Series totals depend on the number of games, availability in each, and playoff minutes inflation.
nba.series_player_exposure.rationale: The draft has a series model for the number of games but no link to each player's exposure, including injuries across games and early eliminations.
nba.series_player_exposure.measurement: E[games] = sum_k k x P(length=k) from nba.series_length_distribution. For player i, exposure_i = sum over games g of P(plays g | length) x E[minutes_g], where P(plays g) follows a two-state Markov chain (available/unavailable) with transition probabilities estimated from playoff games 2010-present by status (initial P from the injury report vintage; persistence P(avail g+1 | absent g) estimated, not fixed at 0.6) and E[minutes_g] = projected regular-season minutes x r from nba.playoff_rotation. Output mean and sd of games played and total minutes by Monte Carlo over the joint series length and availability paths. As-of: injury vintage and completed games.
raw_data: playoff game logs and series lengths
nba.series_player_exposure.why: A total or an average depends on games played, and an average has a random denominator.

nba.playoff_matchup_assignment_shift.label: Playoff matchup assignment shift (primary defender effect)
nba.playoff_matchup_assignment_shift.mechanism: In a series the primary defenders assigned to stars shift counts relative to regular-season rates, adjusted game by game.
nba.playoff_matchup_assignment_shift.rationale: Regular-season position-based opponent allowances miss the specific defender and the series adaptation. The 5-15% shift magnitude is SOURCE_UNVERIFIED (recalled, not estimated).
nba.playoff_matchup_assignment_shift.measurement: For each offensive player O and defender D in the same season compute points per 100 partial possessions guarded (matchup table, min 50 possessions), shrunk to D's overall defensive effect with k=100 possessions and to O's season rate. Series assignment share s_D = 0.5 x share of O's matchup possessions D took in regular-season meetings between the two teams (pooled across seasons if rosters unchanged) + 0.5 x share in playoff games to date (weight rises with games played). Shift = sum_D s_D x (shrunk matchup rate - O's baseline per-100 rate), reported in points and assists per 100, with a standard error from possession counts. Update after each series game with a 2-game half-life; as-of: games completed before tip. Treat the shift as noisy and cap its weight with an out-of-sample test.
raw_data: leagueseasonmatchups: offensive player, defensive player, partial possessions, player points, assists, FGM/FGA allowed
nba.playoff_matchup_assignment_shift.why: Stars' series counts depend on who guards them, but the free source (nba_api leagueseasonmatchups) is a season-type aggregate and game-level playoff assignments are not shown to be available, so the input is context only until the source is verified.

nba.summer_league_game_selection_pattern.label: Summer League game selection and minutes cap pattern
nba.summer_league_game_selection_pattern.mechanism: Participation and minutes in Summer League depend on draft slot, contract status and team plans, with top picks playing fewer games and veterans resting.
nba.summer_league_game_selection_pattern.rationale: Summer League exposure is the main variance of its stat markets, and none of the current inputs gives the probability that a player plays a given game.
nba.summer_league_game_selection_pattern.measurement: Per player: P(plays game g) by draft slot bucket (top 5, 6-14, 15-30, second round, undrafted, veteran) from the last 6 Summer Leagues; minutes distribution per game conditional on playing; adjust for team announcements (coded 0/0.5/1) and for back-to-back games; combine to a distribution of games played and total minutes.
raw_data: Summer League game logs with draft slot
nba.summer_league_game_selection_pattern.why: Summer League props and head-to-heads are decided by participation first.

nba.player_shooting_regression.label: Player shooting luck vs expectation (3P%, FG%, FT%)
nba.player_shooting_regression.mechanism: Hot or cold stretches in 3P%/FG%/FT% mostly regress to a player's shot-quality-adjusted talent, so recent form overstates the next game's expected efficiency.
nba.player_shooting_regression.rationale: Markets and naive models overweight recent hot shooting; true talent is better estimated by priors from career, volume and shot openness. FT% stabilizes faster than 3P%. Subtle: real changes (mechanics, injury recovery, role) exist, so shrinkage weight should depend on sample size and change signals.
nba.player_shooting_regression.measurement: Beta-binomial shrinkage with prior mean = career/role expectation and prior strength set empirically per stat (3P ~ 300-500 att, FT ~ 100-150 att); compare recent vs shrunk estimate; include shot-quality (openness) adjustment.
free_sources: PBPStats.com (free tier: on/off, lineup, possession-level splits)
raw_data: shotchartdetail shot-level rows (zone, action type, result)
nba.player_shooting_regression.why: The compared stat is often made threes (the only live head-to-head series is KXNBAH2H3PT), where three-point shooting luck dominates the variance of the difference and the tie mass; the regression of recent 3P% to talent gives the per-attempt rate.

nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.label: Ratings-based blowout probability and starter-minutes-vs-margin curve (market-free)
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.mechanism: Rebuilds the blowout risk from team strength and rotation history instead of the closing spread: a ratings-implied expected margin and margin spread give P(large lead), and a coach/player minutes-versus-margin curve converts each margin path into expected minutes lost by starters and gained by bench players.
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.rationale: The catalog input nba.garbage is defined from the closing spread, which is a market price and so a benchmark, not an input. The causal quantity is the chance that the margin passes the coach's pull threshold early enough to matter, and how much playing time each player then loses. Subtle: the loss depends on when the lead arrives (a 20-point lead entering Q4 removes far more starter minutes than one reached with 3 minutes left), on the coach, and on whether the trailing team also pulls starters, so the curve must be conditional on the margin path and not only on the final margin.
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.measurement: Step 1, expected margin: mu = (NetRtg_home_adj - NetRtg_away_adj) * expected_possessions/100 + home_adv, where NetRtg_adj is the as-of-tipoff opponent-adjusted net rating from nba.off_rtg and nba.def_rtg (ridge regression on game point differential, half-life about 25 games, shrunk to the preseason prior with n_prior about 20 games as a placeholder to be fitted), adjusted for the confirmed unavailable players via nba.lineup_adj_rating, home_adv fitted on the last 5 seasons (about 2 points). Step 2, margin spread: sd_margin fitted on 5 seasons of residuals of final margin versus mu (league-wide roughly 12-13 points, to be estimated, with a heavier empirical tail than normal). Step 3: P(final |margin| >= 15/20/25) and P(|lead| >= 15/20 entering Q4) from the empirical residual distribution around mu. Step 4, minutes curve: from play-by-play stints, per team-season, expected minutes of each rotation player conditional on margin entering Q4 in bins (0-9, 10-14, 15-19, 20+), shrunk toward the league curve with k about 30 blowout games. Output per player: expected minutes lost and the probability of falling below a stated minutes level. No closing line or other price is used; the spread is retained only to benchmark calibration of step 3.
free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com leaguegamelog (team game logs, free, undocumented, rate-limited)
cdn.nba.com liveData playbyplay JSON (substitutions with score, free, unofficial)
Basketball-Reference game logs and play-by-play (free, polite scraping)
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.why: Replaces the spread-based nba.garbage in player_h2h_series_stats: blowout truncation of the relevant players' minutes from own ratings and the coach's pull curve, with no closing line used.
raw_data: team-game final margins and opponent-adjusted ratings as of tipoff (5 seasons)
play-by-play substitution stints with margin entering Q4

nba.series_stat_leader_model.label: Playoff-series stat-leader probability (max of cumulative totals across both rosters, with ties)
nba.series_stat_leader_model.mechanism: The series leader is the player with the largest cumulative points or rebounds over the series, the maximum of about 16-20 rotation players' totals over a random number of shared games, correlated through series length and pace and negatively within a team.
nba.series_stat_leader_model.rationale: KXNBASERIESPTSLEADER and KXNBASERIESREBLEADER are live under this key and are not pairwise head-to-heads. Leadership concentrates on each team's top producers, and the relevant quantity is the gap in expected per-game rate times games played; summing 4-7 games reduces noise so favourites are stronger than in a single-game leader market, while an injury that costs a candidate one or two games shifts mass sharply. The tie rule is unseen.
nba.series_stat_leader_model.measurement: Simulate each series game by game: series length and winner from nba.series_model; per-player per-game counts from negative-binomial draws on a playoff-minutes scenario (rotation tightening, per-game injury hazard), with per-player rates shrunk to a role prior with k=10 games; compute P(player holds the maximum cumulative total) and P(tie at the maximum) from at least 20,000 simulated series. Calibrate on 15 seasons of playoff series (leader identity against pre-series expected rank, Brier score). As-of: before game 1, then updated after each game with realised totals.
raw_data: playoff player-game box scores (points, rebounds, minutes) for 15 seasons
nba.series_stat_leader_model.why: Series leader markets need the probability of being the maximum among many players' series totals, which pairwise difference inputs do not give.

nba.streak_hit_persistence.label: Game-to-game persistence of threshold hits and streak-break hazard (DNP, rest, matchup)
nba.streak_hit_persistence.mechanism: A streak of N games meeting a threshold is a run-length process whose per-game hit probability varies with minutes and rest and which is broken by any DNP or rest night.
nba.streak_hit_persistence.rationale: Treating hits as independent with the season-average rate understates both streak and break risk; minutes and rest dependencies create positive autocorrelation within a stretch, and the specific rule (whether inactive games break the streak) changes everything.
nba.streak_hit_persistence.measurement: For each player estimate a logistic model of threshold hit on minutes projection, rest days, opponent defensive rating and lag-1 hit (to capture persistence beyond minutes) over a 3-season window; compute probability of a run of length at least N via a Markov chain with state = current run length and per-game hit probability from the model; add break hazard per game from injury/rest model. Adjust for the rule on inactive games (counts as break, skip, or void).
nba.streak_hit_persistence.why: KXNBAPTSALLGAMES is a run of per-game threshold hits over a series that a missed game or cold night breaks, which is exactly the run-length process this input models.
raw_data: player-game points and minutes with rest and DNP flags (3 seasons)

nba.minutes.reason: Minutes in each game feed both players' counts; the distribution differs by setting (playoff vs Summer League) and needs the correlation between the two players' minutes.

nba.usage.reason: Usage is a shot-based opportunity measure; for assists or rebounds comparisons it is the wrong driver, so stat-specific opportunity measures are needed.

nba.stat_dist.reason: Per-stat count marginals are needed for the difference and sum distributions; they do not give dependence between the two players.

nba.injuries_pit.reason: Both players' status is the first gate and, for a series, status over several games with persistence matters.

nba.series_model.reason: Series length distribution is necessary for totals and averages; labelled secondary but it sets exposure and so is primary for series variants.

nba.playoff_rotation.reason: Playoff minute inflation and rotation tightening is a real effect, applying only to the series variant.

nba.summer_league_minutes.reason: Minute plans are central for Summer League but are announced late; the game-selection pattern is a separate factor.

nba.opp_def_pos.reason: Position-based allowances are coarse and unstable, so they act only as the regular-season and Summer League prior; in a series the assigned-defender input is meant to override them, and the matchup interaction tests exactly whether the position prior still carries information.

nba.pace.reason: Shared pace correlates opposing players' counts, which narrows the difference variance; the effect size is modest.

nba.garbage.reason: Catalog definition is 'Blowout / garbage-time probability from spread' (measurement: P(final |margin| > 15/20/25) as a function of the closing spread), so as defined it is market-derived and only a calibration benchmark; the blowout-minutes mechanism is carried by the market-free nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve (ratings-implied margin plus coach minutes-versus-margin curve).

nba.late_game_script.reason: Intentional-foul effects matter for free-throw-related stats only; weak for most compared stats.

m.quote_history.reason: Kalshi price path for the player head-to-head and series stat markets; useful to see when information was absorbed and for calibration labels, but it is an observation of the market, never an explanatory driver of the outcome.

m.rules_text.reason: Versioned rules text defines the settled quantity for the player head-to-head and series stat markets; wording changes between series are the only way to know the target variable, so it is a required contract input, not a feature.

interactions.mechanism: The variance of a difference is var_A + var_B minus twice the covariance, so a positive correlation between opposing players narrows the distribution and raises tie probability, while a negative correlation between teammates widens it; the pair type reverses the effect of the same marginals.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the correlation by pair type and test calibration of P(tie) and P(A>B) on held-out pairs.

interactions.mechanism: A series total is a sum over a random number of games, so a longer series disproportionately raises the upper tail; mean games enter linearly but sd of the total depends on the variance of game counts, which is larger for even matchups than for mismatches.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate series totals under different series length distributions and compare the upper-quantile differences.

interactions.mechanism: If a star is lost for the rest of a series his total stops accumulating and the head-to-head may void; the probability of staying healthy across games declines multiplicatively with persistence, creating a threshold-like drop in total after the first injury.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit a model of games played given injury status after game 1 and compare series totals with and without an injury.

interactions.mechanism: The position-based allowance matters only if the assigned defender follows the position; when a coach assigns a wing stopper to a guard the position average is wrong, so the assignment overrides it.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare predictions using position allowance versus assigned-defender allowance on past series.

interactions.mechanism: A top pick plays a fraction of Summer League games with capped minutes, while a veteran plays all games with full minutes, so stat accumulation is a regime-dependent mixture that depends on the draft-slot bucket.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare per-game minutes and games played across draft-slot buckets for the last six Summer Leagues.

nonlinearities.shape: Discrete, right-skewed series length (4 to 7)
nonlinearities.why: The number of games has a lattice distribution that is bimodal for mismatches and concentrated at 6-7 for even teams, so linearising by an expected length misprices totals.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating minutes inflation near 40
nonlinearities.why: Playoff minutes for stars rise from about 35 to about 40 and cannot rise further, so the inflation factor saturates with role intensity.

nonlinearities.shape: Lattice with a tie mass at zero difference
nonlinearities.why: For low counts (threes, assists) the difference has a notable mass exactly at zero (about 12-20% for threes), so a continuous approximation underprices ties.

nonlinearities.shape: Bimodal minutes (capped versus full)
nonlinearities.why: Summer League minutes cluster at a cap for rookies and at a high value for veterans, so mean minutes are rarely observed.
